title: classical and quantum scattering of massive klein--gordon fields in asymptotically flat spacetimes
abstract: we use microlocal tools to define distinguished incoming and outgoing vacuum states of the quantum theory of massive klein--gordon fields in non-trapping asymptotically flat spacetimes, including radiative perturbations of minkowski space. the asymptotic vacuum states satisfy the hadamard condition, and the incoming and outgoing particle representations are unitarily equivalent, or in other words the quantum s-matrix is well-defined. these results are based on a description of scattering of classical fields which keeps track of the asymptotic distinction between positive- and negative-frequency solutions of the klein--gordon equation. our emphasis is on developing the theory without recourse to explicit asymptotics for classical waves.

title: bilinear products and the orthogonality of quasinormal modes on hyperboloidal foliations
abstract: we explore the properties of bilinear products for black-hole quasinormal modes (qnms) formulated on hyperboloidal foliations. we find that, although qnm solutions are smooth and finite on future-directed hyperboloids, the integrand of the bilinear form with respect to which the modes are orthogonal is still divergent. this is a result of the reflection (equivalently, cpt) transformation required in the definition of the products, which modifies the behaviour of the integrand at the boundaries. we present several regularisation procedures that yield a finite and well-defined bilinear form. in addition, we examine an alternative definition of the bilinear products that incorporates flux contributions, discussing its advantages and limitations. finally, we define the qnm excitation factors and coefficients within the hyperboloidal framework in terms of the bilinear products, and compute them explicitly for a choice of mode numbers and constant initial data. for concreteness, we work with the qnms associated to scalar perturbations of the schwarzschild family of spacetimes.

title: sheaves for spacetimes: a survey
abstract: on a spacetime endowed with a time function (such as a globally hyperbolic manifold) we solve the global cauchy problem for hyperbolic d-modules in the framework of sato's hyperfunctions, illustrating the effectiveness of microlocal-sheaf theoretic methods in linear problems.

title: kerr black holes without primary hairs
abstract: we present a class of regular axisymmetric black hole geometries fully characterized by the parameters $\{{\cal m},a\}$ and possessing the kerr event horizon. this family interpolates between regular spacetimes, configurations with integrable singularities, and the kerr solution as a limiting case. its main features are: (i) the existence of quasi-extremal configurations without requiring $a \approx {\cal m}$; and (ii) a possible framework toward an analytical description of kerr black hole formation from an initially regular configuration.

title: new topological phase transitions in $κ$-deformed $ϕ^4$ lattice models
abstract: this paper explores topological phase transitions in the momentum space of the $κ$-deformed $ϕ^4$ lattice model within the mean-field approximation. we show that the double-well structure of the momentum space gives rise to degenerate momentum states at high energies and that this change is marked by a phase transition. we investigate this transition using both numerical and analytical methods, with the analytical approach based primarily on singularity theory. our numerical analysis shows that the energy at which the topological phase transition occurs is related to the noncommutative parameter by the simple power law $e \sim 1/α^{4}$. by mapping the constant-energy-level surface to the $a_{3}$ singularity, we obtain the same result analytically. we also present results unique to noncommutative systems, showing that the fraction of particles in degenerate momentum states has a nonzero commutative limit. as a nonperturbative effect, this result provides a testable prediction for the existence of noncommutative spacetime.

title: stable manifolds of heteroclinic chains in hořava-lifshitz cosmology
abstract: we consider vacuum spatially homogeneous models in hořava-lifshitz gravity, which are expected to describe generic singularities for these modified gravity theories. these models perturb the well-known bianchi models in general relativity (gr) by a parameter $v\in (0,1)$, in which gr occurs at $v=1/2$. we show that all periodic heteroclinic chains of bianchi type ii orbits are robust for small perturbations of gr, i.e. they exist for any $v\approx 1/2$. moreover, we prove the existence of a stable manifold for each heteroclinic chain within a cantor set for the supercritical case, $v\in (1/2,1)$. in particular, we discuss the heteroclinic chains of periods three and four in detail.

title: hypergeometric solutions to coupled klein-gordon equations in cosmology with small-field excursions
abstract: the klein-gordon equation is a second order differential equation that appears in a variety of applications in mathematics, physics and engineering. this equation is often solved using numerical methods, since a general analytical solution is unattainable. however, one can find very useful analytical solutions for some special cases. in cosmology, the klein-gordon equation of a field can explain the physics of inflation and has important consequences on understanding the origin and evolution of the universe. an analytical solution to the klein-gordon equation in cosmology has been obtained in the small-field excursion approximation, and it turns out that the solution can be written in terms of the confluent hypergeometric limit function. in this work, we derive this result again while showing the details of the calculations and then generalize to the case of two coupled klein-gordon equations. we show that the solution of this coupled system can be written in terms of kummer's hypergeometric limit function while considering minimal assumptions. we carry out a full numerical calculation of the coupled system and compare it to the results from the analytical expressions.

title: suppression of blow-up in the 3d patlak-keller-segel-navier-stokes system via non-parallel shear flows
abstract: in this paper, we consider the three-dimensional patlak-keller-segel system coupled with the navier-stokes equations near the non-parallel shear flow $( ay, 0, ay )$ in $\mathbb{t}\times\mathbb{r}\times\mathbb{t}$. we show that if the shear flow is sufficiently strong (a is large enough), then the solutions to patlak-keller-segel-navier-stokes system are global in time without any smallness restriction on the initial cell mass as long as the initial velocity satisfies $a^{\frac{2}{3}}\|u_{\rm in}\|_{h^2}\leq c_0$, which seems to be the first result of studying the suppression effect of shear flows for the 3d patlak-keller-segel-navier-stokes system. moreover, it implies that the solutions of the 3d navier-stokes equations are global in time if the initial velocity satisfies $a^{\frac{2}{3}}\|v_{\rm in}-(ay,0,ay)\|_{h^2}\leq c_0,$ which also shows the transition threshold for the shear flow $(ay,0,ay)$ in $\mathbb{t}\times\mathbb{r}\times\mathbb{t}$.

title: stability of minkowski-type inequalities in certain warped product spaces
abstract: this paper explores the stability of minkowski-type inequalities for hypersurfaces in warped product spaces. we establish a stability estimate that bounds the norm of the traceless second fundamental form of the hypersurface in terms of the deficit in the minkowski inequalities satisfied by the hypersurface. additionally, we prove the stability of minkowski inequalities in specific cases of the reissner-nordström anti-de sitter (rn-ads) and anti-de sitter schwarzschild (ads-schwarzschild) manifolds, which serve as examples of warped products. we also establish a new rigidity result for locally conformally flat manifolds to understand the stability of these inequalities.

title: local asymptotics for singular solutions to critical hartree equations
abstract: for $n\geqslant3$ and $0<α<n$, we study positive classical solutions of critical hartree equations that blow up at the origin. for the global problem on $\mathbb r^n\setminus\{0\}$, with the hartree potential integrated over $\mathbb r^n$, we prove that solutions in $l^p(\mathbb r^n)$, where $p=(n+α)/(n-2)$, are radial and nonincreasing in $|x|$. we establish an integral representation and apply moving spheres to this nonlocal problem. for the local problem on $b_r\setminus\{0\}$, with the hartree potential integrated over $b_r$, we prove $u(x)\leqslant c|x|^{-(n-2)/2}$ near the origin and \begin{equation*}   u(x)=\bar u(|x|)\bigl(1+\mathcal o(|x|)\bigr)\qquad\text{as }x\to0, \end{equation*} where $\bar u$ is the spherical average of $u$. a main difficulty is controlling the nonlocal hartree potential under kelvin inversion and in the blow-up limit. the local proof combines blow-up analysis and moving spheres with estimates of the integral tails and an auxiliary liouville lemma. we also give an alternative proof of the classification of positive $c^2$ solutions of the critical hartree equation in $\mathbb r^n$.

title: transverse dependence and asymptotic dimensional reduction of ground states for the logarithmic schrödinger equation on a waveguide manifold
abstract: in this paper, we develop a novel approach to studying the $y$-dependence of ground states for the logarithmic schrödinger equation on $\mathbb{r}^d \times \mathbb{t}$. unlike in \cite{stnt2014} (analysis \& pde, 2014) and \cite{hh1} (siam j. math. anal., 2024), the power-law scaling argument does not transfer directly to the logarithmic setting. instead, amplitude scaling gives an exact identity showing that transverse dependence is independent of the prescribed mass. we also discuss uniqueness for the cauchy problem and conditional orbital stability.

title: multiple positive bound states for nls equations on noncompact metric graphs with potential
abstract: in this paper, we establish the existence of geometrically distinct bound states for the subcritical nonlinear schrödinger (nls) equation on a noncompact metric graph, provided that the mass is sufficiently large. by bound states we mean critical points of the nls energy functional constrained to the manifold of fixed $l^2$-norm. we demonstrate that the nls equation admits at least as many positive bound states as the number of bounded edges of the graph. our approach is purely variational and relies on a doubly constrained minimization procedure. it is worth noting that, compared with the case where the potential vanishes, the scaling structure of solitons is destroyed here. moreover, the classical energy asymptotic behavior $\mathcal{e}(ϕ_μ,\mathbb{r})=-θμ^{2β+1}$ is no longer preserved.

title: inverse problems for the monge-ampère equation: linearization and nonlinear recovery
abstract: we study inverse boundary value problems for the fully nonlinear monge-ampère equation $ \det d^2u=a(x,u,\nabla u) $ in a bounded domain. motivated by calderón-type problems, we introduce nonlinear cauchy data and investigate the recovery of $a$ from boundary measurements. around a strictly convex background solution, under a sign condition ensuring invertibility of the linearized dirichlet problem, we establish local well-posedness and differentiable dependence on boundary data. the first variation yields a linear elliptic operator with principal coefficient given by the cofactor of the background hessian and lower-order coefficients determined by derivatives of $a$. an alessandrini-type identity reduces equality of nonlinear measurements to an anisotropic calderón problem. conditional on uniqueness for this linear problem, we recover the first derivatives of $a$ along the background jet. higher-order linearization yields integral identities whose inversion depends on a product-density property. we also establish unconditional uniqueness results in special settings. for $\det d^2u=f(x)$, local nonlinear cauchy data determine $f$ in dimension two, and in higher dimensions under real-analytic anisotropic hypotheses. we compare this result with a planar small-data method and an all-dimensional large-data approach based on the euclidean x-ray transform. for semilinear nonlinearities around $φ(x)=|x|^2/2$, schrödinger inverse results recover the accessible $z$-jet. for equilibrium optimal-transport nonlinearities, linearization yields an isotropic conductivity equation and uniquely determines the transport density.

title: logarithmic depletion of vortex stretching and singularity evasion in the 3d navier-stokes equations
abstract: we present a geometric-analytic mechanism for the suppression of finite-time singularities in the 3d incompressible (unforced) navier-stokes equations for critical point singularities exhibiting $l^{3/2, \infty}$ spatial concentration of vorticity. we demonstrate that if the vorticity direction resides locally in a logarithmically weighted space of bounded mean oscillations, $\mathrm{bmo}_{1/|\log r|}$ -- a space failing the dini condition and thus permitting wild oscillatory defects -- the nonlinear vortex stretching is fundamentally depleted. by isolating a unidirectional geometric cancellation, we recast the stretching eigenvalue as a singular integral commutator. utilizing a localized coifman-rochberg-weiss estimate coupled with dyadic bmo tail bounds, we prove the stretching potential vanishes as a logarithmic envelope on shrinking super-level sets. this depletion forces the vorticity magnitude into a sub-critical lorentz-zygmund space via interpolated de giorgi energy method. the logarithmic gain is subsequently transferred to the velocity field, forcing the geometric scale of local 1d sparseness below the uniform radius of spatial analyticity, ultimately averting the finite time blow-up via the harmonic measure maximum principle.

title: pper and lower bounds for blow-up times in coupled reaction--diffusion systems with nonlocal sources
abstract: in this paper, we consider the following reaction-diffusion system \begin{equation*} \begin{cases}   u_t=δu+f\bigl(x,t,u,v,v(t)\bigr), & (x,t)\in\om\times(0,t),   v_t=δv+g\bigl(x,t,u,v,u(t)\bigr), & (x,t)\in\om\times(0,t),   \mathcal b u=\mathcal b v=0, & (x,t)\in\partial\om\times(0,t),   u(x,0)=u_0(x),\quad v(x,0)=v_0(x), & x\in\om, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where \begin{equation*}   u(t)=\int_{\om}u(x,t)\dd x,\qquad   v(t)=\int_{\om}v(x,t)\dd x, \end{equation*} and the boundary operator $\mathcal b$ is either \[   \mathcal b_d w=w   \qquad\text{or}\qquad   \mathcal b_n w=\partial_νw, \] $\om\subset\r^n$ be a bounded domain with sufficiently smooth boundary, $n\ge 1$, and $ν$ is the outward unit normal on $\partial\om$.   under certain conditions, we obtain the upper and lower bounds for the blowup time of the solution to the system.

title: spectral gårding elliptic equations
abstract: we study spectral gårding elliptic equations on compact kähler manifolds. smooth solvability is equivalent to the existence of a smooth representative in the admissible domain. the concavity theorem for ideal gårding polynomials gives a fixed concave formulation to which székelyhidi's second-order argument applies in every degree $2\le d\le n$, extending lin's top-degree solvability theorem. combined with the numerical criteria of fu--li--zhang--zhang and chen--nie--xu, this yields a nakai--moishezon type criterion for solvability on compact kähler manifolds.   a solution converts the local ideal gårding structure into a global lorentzian structure. its mixed derivatives give a strict nonlinear hodge--riemann hierarchy from the degree of the equation down to degree two, and the homogenization of the intersection polynomial is lorentzian in nef class directions. numerical criteria then produce explicit hodge--riemann classes, lefschetz isomorphisms in bidegree $(1,1)$, and weighted hodge-index inequalities.

title: classification of minimal-mass blowup solutions to the mass-critical hartree equation at the $l^2$-critical level
abstract: in this paper, we study the focusing mass-critical hartree equation \[ iu_t+δu=-\bigl(|x|^{-2}*|u|^2\bigr)u \] at the ground-state mass $m(q)$. we prove that, up to the symmetries of the equation, every global minimal-mass non-scattering solution is a solitary wave, while every finite-time minimal-mass blowup solution is a pseudo-conformal image of a solitary wave. this extends the results of \cite{lz28,miao-xu-zhao3,wang-gao} to the scaling-critical space $l^2$ and removes the radial assumption in the global case.

title: orbital stability of solitary wave solutions of the derivative nonlinear schrödinger equation in the endpoint case
abstract: in this paper, we consider the orbital stability of solitary waves for the derivative nonlinear schrödinger equation $$iq_t+q_{xx}+i\partial_x\bigl(|q|^2q\bigr)=0, \quad (t,x)\in\mathbb{r}\times\mathbb{r}.$$ for the endpoint solitary waves satisfying $c>0$ and $c^2=4ω$, we prove the orbital stability in $h^1(\mathbb{r})$ without any additional assumptions. the proof uses conservation of mass and the second hamiltonian $\mathcal{h}_2$ to keep the bäcklund-transformed solution small in $h^1(\mathbb{r})$ uniformly in time. we establish an inverse bäcklund compactness result to reconstruct the algebraic solitary wave as the spectral zero approaches the negative real axis.

title: a viscoelastic wave equation with nonlinear damping and supercritical variable-exponent logarithmic sources
abstract: we investigate a viscoelastic wave equation with nonlinear variable-exponent damping and a variable-exponent logarithmic source, allowing supercritical growth. the main difficulties arise from the failure of the source to map the energy space into $l^2(ω)$, the sign-changing logarithmic potential, and the lack of sobolev control of the displacement for supercritical damping. under an exponent condition linking the source and damping exponents, we prove local existence, an energy identity, and a continuation criterion. we prove finite-time blow-up for nontrivial solutions with nonpositive shifted initial energy. we also establish a blow-up criterion based on a sufficiently large initial displacement--velocity pairing, with a threshold depending on the positive part of the shifted initial energy, and derive an explicit upper bound for the lifespan. this criterion allows us to construct blow-up data at every prescribed level of the original energy. for initial data in a suitable stable region, solutions exist globally. for damping within the sobolev range, a general relaxation condition yields energy decay estimates that include exponential and polynomial rates. beyond this range, a time-weighted displacement estimate and a splitting of the memory integral give logarithmic decay.

title: the cr nirenberg problem, part ii: existence and topological degree
abstract: this paper is a continuation of part~i \cite{qtwparti}, where blow-up analysis and compactness results for the cr nirenberg problem were established. we prove some existence and degree results for the cr nirenberg problem on the standard sphere. more precisely, we first prove existence results under antipodal and, more generally, finite-group symmetries. without symmetry, we derive a leray--schauder degree formula under natural flatness conditions, yielding existence results for positive prescribed curvatures with certain homogeneous expansions at critical points. we also obtain aubin-type inequalities under a vanishing first-moment condition, uniformly near the critical exponent.

title: sharp conditions for fully nonlinear equations with $(n-1)$-hessian matrix: part ii. $k$-hessian case
abstract: we study admissible entire subsolutions and radial boundary blow-up solutions of $s_k^{\frac1k}[δui-d^2u]=f(u)+g(u)|du|^q$ for $1\leq k<n$, continuing our study of the determinant case $k=n$ in part i. under structural assumptions on the continuous, non-decreasing coefficients $f$ and $g$, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of entire subsolutions when $q<2$. our results cover the non-lipschitz case $0<q<1$ with a possibly vanishing zero-order term, the gradient-singular case $q<0$, and sign-changing gradient coefficients. we also characterize finite-radius blow-up of radial solutions and derive two-sided estimates for the blow-up radius, as well as pointwise upper bounds for their profiles in terms of inverse keller--osserman functions.

title: an optimization problem for $δ'$ leaky stars
abstract: we consider singular schrödinger operators with an attractive $δ'$ interaction of strength $β$ supported by a star graph and prove that the ground-state eigenvalue is uniquely maximized by stars of the maximum symmetry. two different proofs are presented, one for an even number of edges using a comparison to the $δ$ interaction star, the other general based on birman-schwinger technique.

title: (super-)fast convergence rates for chernoff approximations via centered differences and richardson extrapolation
abstract: we use centered differences to construct chernoff families and derive even asymptotic expansions for their iterated products. richardson extrapolation is then used to cancel polynomial part and thereby raise the convergence order. as illustrations, we apply the construction to uniformly parabolic, schrödinger-type second-order operators and to a third-order dispersive operator, obtaining, at extrapolation depth $m$, the rates $ o(n^{-2m}) $ on the sobolev scales $h^{2m+δ}$, $h^{4m}$, and $h^{5m}$, respectively, with arbitrary $δ>0$. in the analytic category, quantitative all-order estimates allow the extrapolation depth to grow with the base resolution and yield the super-fast rates $e^{-cn^2}$ for the two second-order models and $e^{-cn} $ for the third-order model. the constructions are explicit in terms of the coefficients of the underlying differential operators and do not use the target semigroup in their definition. this provides a constructive positive answer to the challenge of super-fast chernoff approximation formulated by remizov in problem 30 of arxiv:2410.00416.

title: boundary regularity for fractional porous medium-type equations in bounded domains
abstract: we prove boundary hölder regularity for fractional porous medium-type equations in bounded smooth domains with zero exterior data. for $0<σ<1$, $n>2σ$, and $m>1$, we show that nonnegative weak dual solutions $v$ of $\partial_t v+(-δ)^σ(v^m)=0$ satisfy \[ \frac{v}{d^{σ/m}}\in c_{x,t}^{α,\frac{αm}{σ(m+1)}} \] up to the boundary and away from the initial time, for some $α\in(0,σ)$, where $d$ denotes the distance to the boundary. more generally, we establish boundary hölder estimates for $u/d^σ$ for nonnegative viscosity solutions of $\partial_t u=u^γlu$, with $0<γ<1$ and initial data comparable to $d^σ$. here $l$ is a symmetric stable operator of order $2σ$ whose measurable angular density is bounded above and below by positive constants. our proof combines comparison principles and boundary barriers with a blow-up and compactness argument based on a liouville theorem for ancient solutions in a half-space.

title: weighted and sobolev estimates for fractional schrödinger operators with reverse hölder potentials
abstract: we study weighted and sobolev estimates for two fractional schrödinger operators on $\mathbb{r}^n$, where $n\geq3$ and $0<s<1$. for the additive operator $l=(-δ)^s+v$, with a nonnegative, nontrivial potential $v$ belonging to a suitable reverse hölder class, $rh_q$, we establish a critical-radius form inequality and decay estimates for the semigroup mass. these yield a heat-kernel bound combining polynomial off-diagonal decay with a fixed positive exponent of decay relative to the fractional critical radius $ρ_s$. a decomposition at this scale gives weighted strong-type estimates for the semigroup maximal operator and weighted hardy--littlewood--sobolev estimates for $l^{-α/2}$, $0<αs<n$, together with the corresponding endpoint weak-type estimates. the admissible weights satisfy explicit growth restrictions determined by the kernel decay, and the fractional integration order is $αs$. we also consider the spectral operator $q=(-δ+v)^s$. assuming $v\in rh_{q_1}$ with $n/(1+s)\leq q_1<n$ and classical critical radius $ρ_1(x)\geq1$, we prove that $\nabla q^{-1/2}$ maps $h^{1-s,p}(\mathbb{r}^n)$ into $l^p(\mathbb{r}^n)$ for $1<p\leq p_0$, where $1/p_0=1/q_1-1/n$. by duality, its adjoint   maps $l^{p^{'}}(\mathbb{r}^n)$ into $h^{s-1,p^{'}}(\mathbb{r}^n)$ for $p_0^{'}\leq p^{'}<\infty$.

title: asymptotic stability and sharp decay near homogeneous solutions of a nonlinearly damped schrödinger equation on the torus
abstract: we study the one-dimensional periodic nonlinear schrödinger equation with a power-type nonlinear damping, both in the focusing and the defocusing regime. for a sufficiently small damping parameter and initial data close in relative $h^1$ norm to a nonzero spatially homogeneous state, we prove global existence and asymptotic convergence, after a constant phase adjustment, to an explicit homogeneous solution. the \(l^2\) and \(h^1\) norms follow the explicit adiabatic decay law, with the same leading coefficient as the homogeneous solution. we obtain explicit convergence rates, including a \(t^{-1/2}\) bound for the relative spatial perturbation. for every nonconstant initial datum in a small neighborhood of the homogeneous solution, the kinetic energy has a strictly positive leading coefficient and decays one power of time faster than the squared \(l^2\) norm.

title: long-time asymptotics for the focusing coupled kundu-eckhaus equation
abstract: the focusing coupled kundu-eckhaus (cke) equation extends the coupled nonlinear schrödinger (cnls) equation by adding quintic and derivative nonlinearities. we study the cauchy problem for the focusing cke equation with schwartz initial data under the assumption of no discrete spectrum and no spectral singularities on the real axis. based on the gauge equivalence between the focusing cke and cnls equations, we analyze the associated $3\times3$ matrix riemann-hilbert problem by the deift-zhou nonlinear steepest descent method. by establishing joint error estimates for the cnls solution and the gauge phase, we obtain a uniform long-time asymptotic formula for the dispersive radiation of the cke equation with an $o(t^{-1}\log t)$ remainder in bounded velocity cones.

title: minimal time for heat observability on almost-riemannian surfaces
abstract: we determine the minimal observation time for the heat equation on a closed almost-riemannian surface, for a class of observation sets leaving sufficiently thin collars around simple baouendi-grushin circles. the structure and density are analytic near these circles, and the coefficients may depend on both variables. the formula is expressed through a complex phase describing concentration near the singular set and extends the thresholds known for separated models. regular unobserved regions away from the circles do not change this time, provided all other singularities are observed. for singular circles of constant bracket step greater than two, local analyticity implies failure of observability at every time for observation sets at positive distance. we also construct quasimodes concentrated near simple singular circles, with exponentially small errors. their superpositions give a lower bound for the schrödinger observation time.

title: gauge transforms and strichartz estimates for benjamin--ono-type dirac equations
abstract: for $t>0$, we consider the benjamin--ono-type dirac equation $$ i\partial_tψ(x,t) + d(-δ)^{\frac{1}{2}}ψ(x,t) = d\,g(ψ(x,t)), \qquad (x,t)\in\mathbb{r}^n\times[0,t], $$ where $(-δ)^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is the fractional riesz operator, $d$ is the dirac operator associated with the clifford algebra of signature $(0,n)$, and $g(\cdot)$ a scalar-valued quadratic nonlinearity. under a pointwise anti-commutation condition on $ψ$ and a uniform dyadic regularity assumption on its spatial fourier profile, we construct a unit-modulus gauge map $u$ by $ u=\exp\bigl(-iw\bigr),$ where $w$ is a solution of $dw=ψ$. assuming, in addition, the stated regularity and commutation conditions on $w$, we show that the plemelj components $u_{\pm}=p_{\pm}u$ solve a coupled schrödinger system with gauge nonlinearities $p_{\pm}n(ψ,u)$, where $$ n(ψ(x,t),u(x,t)) = -2p_{-}\!\left[ g(ψ(x,t)) \right]u(x,t). $$ we also obtain a priori estimates for the homogeneous sobolev seminorms $\dot h^σ$ of $ψ(\cdot,t)$, with at most exponential growth on $[0,t]$, together with estimates for $p_{\pm}n(ψ(\cdot,t),u(\cdot,t))$. combining these bounds with the homogeneous and inhomogeneous strichartz estimates for the schrödinger system, we obtain, for $n\geq 3$ and every sharp schrödinger admissible pair $(q,p)$, an a priori strichartz-type estimate for $ψ$ in $l_t^q\dot w_x^{σ,p}$, expressed in terms of the initial datum $ψ(\cdot,0)$ and the a priori controls of $ψ$ in $l_t^\infty h_x^{σ+1}$ and $l_t^\infty l_x^\infty$.

title: limit cycles govern wave energy accumulation in space-time-varying materials
abstract: we study the amplification and concentration of wave energy in smooth, periodic space-time media through the dynamics of the characteristic curves of the associated wave equation. in an impedance-matched setting, we show that stable limit cycles attract neighbouring characteristics, focusing the wave energy density. the exponential attraction rate is estimated analytically from the system's lyapunov exponent. we further show that the attraction of characteristics and energy accumulation persist under a range of nonperiodic perturbations. finally, we present a floquet-fourier numerical method for computing stable and unstable limit cycles and their attraction rates. throughout, we exemplify the results using the example of modulation given by a superposition of travelling waves, revealing saddle--node bifurcations where limit cycles may appear depending on the relative wave speeds. full-wave simulations confirm that the characteristic mechanism continues to describe energy accumulation beyond the impedance-matched case.

title: local well-posedness for the exponentially modified benjamin-ono equation
abstract: we prove local well-posedness for the modified benjamin-ono equation in $h^s(\mathbb{r})$ for $s>3/2$. this equation arises as a modified counterpart of the benjamin-ono equation through a miura-type transformation, in close analogy with the classical relation between mkdv and kdv equations. one of the main obstacles is the apparent derivative loss in the quadratic part of the equation. to overcome this difficulty, we introduce a cole-hopf transform adapted to the structure of the equation. the map removes the quadratic derivative term and converts the equation into a schrödinger equation with a transport and a commutator terms that can be controlled without derivative loss. solutions are then constructed by parabolic regularization, while frequency envelopes are used to obtain the continuity of the data-to-solution map. in the degenerate case $γ=0$, the transform completely linearizes the equation and yields local well-posedness for every $s>1/2$, down to the scaling-critical threshold.

title: multi-peak solutions for a magnetic nonlinear schrödinger equation with exponential critical growth in $\mathbb{r}^{2}$
abstract: in this paper, we study the following magnetic nonlinear schrödinger equation \[ \left(\frac{\varepsilon}{i}\nabla-a(x)\right)^{2}u+v(x)u=f(|u|^{2})u\,\ \text{in}\,\ \mathbb{r}^{2}, \] where $\varepsilon>0$ is a parameter, $a\in c(\mathbb{r}^{2}, \mathbb{r}^{2})$ is a magnetic potential, $v\in c(\mathbb{r}^{2}, \mathbb{r})$ is a multi-well potential, and $f\in c^1(\mathbb{r}, \mathbb{r})$ exhibits exponential critical growth. by variational methods and a penalization technique, we prove the existence and multiplicity of nontrivial solutions for sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. if, in addition, $a\in c^1(\mathbb{r}^2,\mathbb{r}^2)$, we show that these solutions have multiple peaks and we establish their concentration behavior and exponential decay.

title: what remains when integrability fails? mathematical structure in the k(m,m) compacton equations
abstract: peter lax's 1968 discovery that certain nonlinear wave equations possess operator pairs (lax pairs) opened the theory of completely integrable systems, yielding exact solutions, infinite conservation hierarchies, and perfectly elastic soliton collisions. when a nonlinear dispersive equation is provably non-integrable (admitting no lax pair and only finitely many conservation laws), what mathematical structure governs its dynamics?   the k(m,m) compacton equations, u_t + (u^m)_x + (u^m)_{xxx} = 0 for m >= 2, provide a testing ground: they support traveling waves with compact support, yet fail every known integrability test. we prove universal algebraic formulas determining the shape, width, and speed of every k(m,m) compacton. we develop a constraint-deficit mechanism explaining how the five independent conservation laws constrain emergent amplitudes and suppress the fundamental fourier mode of the collision debris, while higher radiation modes remain unconstrained. the mechanism's conclusions rest on explicit hypotheses supported by numerical evidence. a phase-plane analysis reveals the compacton as a singular limit of smooth solitary waves through simultaneous regularity loss and support compactification. these results delineate intermediate territory between integrable order and generic nonlinear dynamics, organized by scaling universality and by the constraint deficit of a finite conservation structure.

title: sharp damping location for stability of a locally damped wave equation and its galerkin approximation
abstract: we study the stability of the variable coefficient wave equation $u_{tt}-u_{xx}-(1+x^{2})u_{yy}+χ_{\mathbb g}u_{t}=0$ on the rectangle $(-1,1)\times(0,π)$ with dirichlet boundary conditions, where the viscous damping acts on a vertical strip $\mathbb g=(η-δ,η+δ)\times(0,π)$. we establish a precise relationship between the location of the damping region and the rate of energy decay. we prove that the associated semigroup is exponentially stable whenever the closure of the damping strip meets the line $x=0$, i.e., $|η|\leqδ$, despite the existence of rays that never enter the damped region. when the damping region is strictly bounded away from $x=0$, the semigroup decays at the sharp rate $(\log(2+t))^{-1}$. the proofs combine separation of variables, one-dimensional resolvent estimates, a reflection identity for the harmonic oscillator, and gaussian quasimodes. we then consider the spectral galerkin approximation based on the dirichlet eigenfunctions of the constant coefficient laplacian and show that, although the sequence of semigroups resulting from the approximation converges to the continuous one, it fails to be uniformly exponentially stable.

title: global existence of the $s$-schrödinger maps in $n \geq 5$
abstract: we study the $s$-schrödinger map equation \[ \begin{cases} \partial_t u = -u \wedge (-δ)^s u   \quad \text{on } \mathbb{r}^n \times \mathbb{r}\\ u: \mathbb{r}^n \times \mathbb{r} \to \mathbb{s}^2\\ u(x,0) = u_0. \end{cases} \] for $s \in (1/2,1)$ and $n \geq 5$ we prove that for small initial data $u_0$ in the critical besov space one can obtain a global solution.

title: ground states of a logarithmic schrödinger equation with a power perturbation in $\mathbb{r}^n$: existence, uniqueness and nondegeneracy
abstract: the objective of this paper is to study the existence and uniqueness of positive ground state solutions of the following schrödinger problem \[   -δu=u\log u^2+μ\abs{u}^{p-1}u\qquad\text{in }\mathbb {r}^n, \] where $n\ge2$, $1<p<2^*-1$ and $μ>0.$ we prove that there exists a positive ground state solution for every $μ>0$ and every such solution is smooth, radially symmetric with respect to some point, strictly decreasing in the radial variable. moreover, as $μ\downarrow0,$ the positive ground state solutions centered at the origin will converge, uniformly over the ground-state set, to $u_0(x)=\exp(\frac{(n-\abs{x}^2)}{2})$ in the logarithmic orlicz--sobolev space and in $c^{2,α}(\r^n)$ for every $α\in(0,1),$ respectively. furthermore, for sufficiently small $μ,$ we also prove that the positive ground state solutions are unique up to translations and the kernel space of the real scalar linearized operator can be spanned by the translation derivatives. the proof combines minimization on the nehari manifold with uniform compactness and an exterior coefficient estimate that prevents normalized difference and kernel sequences from vanishing locally.

title: cubic nonlinear schrödinger systems and orthonormal fermionic ground states in $\mathbb r$
abstract: we study the one-dimensional nonlinear schrödinger system \[ -u_i''-2\big(\sum_{k=1}^n u_k^2\big)^{p-1}u_i=μ_i u_i \quad \mbox{in } \ \mathbb r,\ \ i=1,2,\cdots,n, \tag{s} \] where $u=(u_1,\cdots,u_n)\in h^1(\mathbb{r})^n$, $μ_1\leqμ_2\leq\cdots\leqμ_n<0$, $1<p<3$ and $n\geq 2$ are arbitrary. for the cubic case where $p=2$ and $n\ge 2$, we establish the following structural results of the system $(s)$: (i) all nontrivial solutions can be classified completely; (ii) the linearized operator at any nontrivial solution is non-degenerate; (iii) exact $l^2$-mass formulas of all nontrivial solutions are derived in terms of distinct lagrange multipliers $μ_i$. as the applications of the above structural results, we first show that the system $(s)$ with $p=2$ does not have any orthonormal solution for any $n\ge2$. we then investigate a fermionic variational problem $j_n(p)$ with $n\ge2$, whose minimizers correspond to ground states of the system $(s)$ under orthonormal constraints. more precisely, we prove that there exists a sufficiently small $δ_n>0$ such that $j_n(p)$ is attained for any $p\in(2-δ_n,2)$, whereas $j_n(p)$ is not attained for any $p\in[2,2+δ_n)$. these settle some conjectures of [gontier--lewin--nazar, arma, 2021] and [frank--gontier--lewin, cmp, 2021].

title: existence of solution for schrödinger-newton system with vanishing magnetic potential
abstract: in this paper, we study the following schrödinger-newton system with a vanishing magnetic potential and an electric potential \begin{equation}\label{0.1} \left\{   \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.25}   \begin{array}{ll}   (-i\nabla +a(x))^2u+v(x)u=φu, \ & x\in\mathbb{r}^3,\\ -δφ=|u|^2, \ & x\in\mathbb{r}^3,   \end{array}   \right. \end{equation} where $i$ is the imaginary unit, $a:\mathbb{r}^3\to \mathbb{r}^3$ is a continuous magnetic potential, and $v:\mathbb{r}^3\to \mathbb{r}$ is a continuous electric potential. first, we show that the ground state energy of system with $a(x)\equiv0$ and $v(x)\equiv v_{\infty}>0$ is isolated. using this fact together with a global compactness lemma, a barycenter function, and brouwer degree theory, we prove that under suitable conditions on $a$ and $v$, system admits either a ground state solution or a high energy solution. interestingly, whether a ground state solution exists is significantly affected by the magnetic potential $a$ and the electric potential $v$. furthermore, we provide sufficient conditions that guarantee the existence of a ground state solution, as well as conditions under which no ground state solution exists and a high energy solution appears instead.

title: eigenvalue fluctuations for the crushed ice problem
abstract: we study the eigenvalues of the negative dirichlet laplacian $-δ$ in domain $d_{ε,n}$ obtained by removing $n$ euclidean balls of radius $ε$ from a bounded open set $d\subseteq\mathbb r^d$ ($d\ge2$). it is known that, for the balls centered at points drawn independently from a distribution with probability density $ρ$ and for $n\to\infty$ and $ε\downarrow0$ so that the aggregate newtonian capacity of the removed balls tends to some $κ>0$, the eigenvalues of $-δ$ in $d_{ε,n}$ homogenize to those of the schrödinger operator $-δ+κρ$ in $d$. here we prove that, for the eigenvalues that are simple in the limit, a multivariate central limit theorem holds in all $d\ge2$ under centering by expected values. unlike earlier work in $d=3$ by figari, orlandi and teta and, independently, ozawa from 1980s that was based on resolvent expansions, we rely on martingale representations and one-ball perturbation asymptotic controlled by methods of harmonic analysis.

title: orthonormal strichartz estimates over fractal time
abstract: we study strichartz estimates for orthonormal families of initial data when time is integrated against an $α$-dimensional frostman measure $μ$, $0<α\le1$, with coefficients measured in $\ell^β$. for the fractional schrödinger, wave and klein--gordon equations, we obtain orthogonality gains in the admissible region and necessary conditions on $β$. for the fractional schrödinger equation the exponents are sharp up to an endpoint; the optimality of the threshold $β=q/2$ requires $μ$ to be ahlfors regular. for the schrödinger equation in dimensions $d\ge2$, we prove a lorentz endpoint estimate and, if $d>2α$, the critical exponent $β=q/2$ at every pair $2\le q,r<\infty$ with \[\frac d2(\frac12-\frac1r)\ge\fracαq, \quad r>\frac{dq}{d-α};\] on $r=\infty$ we obtain a restricted weak-type estimate. since the constants depend on $μ$ only through its frostman constant, lebesgue measure yields global-in-time critical estimates in this range when $d\ge3$. the proofs combine frostman fractional integration, a spectral near--far argument at the endpoint, and asymmetric hilbert--schmidt bounds with orthogonal frequency-block summation. we also obtain further estimates in the low-dimensional cases $d=1$ (fractional schrödinger) and $d=2$ (wave and klein--gordon) with $α>1/2$, and formulate the consequences for densities of freely evolving states.

title: blowup of smooth solutions to 2d quasilinear wave equations with higher-order null conditions and short pulse initial data
abstract: this paper investigates the 2d quasilinear wave equation $\displaystyle\sum_{α,β=0}^{2}g^{αβ}(\partialϕ)\partial_{αβ}^{2}ϕ=0$ with the short pulse initial data $(ϕ, \partial_tϕ)|_{t=1}=(δ^{2-\varepsilon_0}ϕ_0(\frac{r-1}δ,ω), δ^{1-\varepsilon_0}ϕ_1(\frac{r-1}δ,ω))$, where $0<\varepsilon_0<1$ is a fixed constant and $δ>0$ is a small parameter. in our previous work [ding bingbing, xin zhouping, yin huicheng, sci. china math., vol. 69 (2026), no. 3, 667-736], we have established the global existence of a smooth solution $ϕ$ under the $k$-th order null condition ($k\ge 2$) when the $(k+1)$-th order null condition fails, provided that $0<\varepsilon_0<\varepsilon_k^*=\frac{k}{k+1}$. as a natural continuation, the present paper demonstrates that for $\varepsilon_0\ge \varepsilon_k^*$, the smooth solution $ϕ$ blows up in finite time. consequently, the threshold $\varepsilon_0=\varepsilon_k^*$ is shown to be the critical exponent that precisely characterizes the global existence and finite-time blowup for smooth short pulse solutions to the aforementioned 2d quasilinear wave equation, under the assumption that the $k$-th order null condition holds while the $(k+1)$-th order null condition does not. a key novelty of our approach lies in deriving sharp orders of $δ$ for almost all quantities in both energy and pointwise estimates. this is achieved by utilizing the higher-order null structure in conjunction with a new good unknown recently introduced by us and the transport equation for the difference between this good unknown and its corrector.

title: acoustic gravitational waves beyond leading order in bubble over hubble radius
abstract: we calculate the gravitational wave power spectrum from sound waves in a cosmological first order phase transition in the unexplored regime of large bubbles, by which we mean that the mean bubble spacing $r_*$ is a non-negligible fraction of the hubble length $\mathcal{h}_*^{-1}$, i.e. $r_*\mathcal{h}_* \lesssim \mathcal{o}(1)$. since the amplitude of the gravitational wave signal increases with $r_*\mathcal{h}_*$, this is also the loud signal regime. in this regime the effects of gravity, hitherto neglected, become relevant. we carry out the calculation in cosmological perturbation theory expanding in the parameter $r_*\mathcal{h}_*$, or bubble over hubble radius. the leading order term is the standard result for acoustic production of gravitational waves. at next-to-leading order we find three novel contributions: two contributions arise from general relativistic corrections to the dynamics of both sound and gravitational waves. a third contribution comes from gravitational waves induced by curvature perturbations. these contributions suppress the gravitational wave peak amplitude. the suppression factor, with respect to the leading order contribution, scales as $(r_*\mathcal{h}_*)^2$, and also depends on other transition parameters, such as the sound speed $c_s$, the duration of the acoustic source, and the peak wavenumber of the velocity field $k_p$. in a simplified model of the velocity field, we find that the suppression factor lies between $2\%$ and $15\%$ when $r_*\mathcal{h}_* \simeq 0.5$, but is independent of the root mean squared fluid velocity. we provide analytical approximations to the next-to-leading order corrections, and a recipe to join them smoothly across different frequency regimes. our work improves the precision of the current estimations of the gravitational wave power spectrum in the relatively unexplored regime of phase transition with large bubbles.

title: mergers fall short: non-merger channels required for galactic heavy element production
abstract: since the discovery of the binary neutron star merger gw170817 and its associated kilonova, neutron star mergers have been established as a key production channel for r-process elements in the universe. however, various lines of evidence, including observations of r-process abundances inferred from stellar spectra of milky way disk stars, suggest that additional channels are needed to fully account for r-process element enrichment in the milky way. neutron star-black hole mergers and fast-merging binary neutron star systems are among the leading alternative candidates. in this paper, we combine gravitational-wave observations from ligo-virgo-kagra with data from short gamma-ray bursts, galactic pulsars, and galactic eu/fe versus fe/h abundance observations to assess the contribution of these mergers to r-process enrichment in the galactic disk. our analysis employs a unified, likelihood-based inference framework that consistently propagates uncertainties in merger rates, delay-time distributions, mass- and spin-dependent ejecta yields, and stellar abundance measurements. we find that neither neutron star-black hole mergers nor fast- merging binary neutron star populations can serve as the dominant additional channel without generating strong tension with existing observations and theoretical expectations. these results constrain the viable sources of galactic r-process enrichment and underscore the necessity of non- merger production channels.

title: sound wave in the backreaction affected spacetime in analogue gravity based on number-conserving approach
abstract: adopting a number-conserving approach, we show that the sound wave in the backreaction-affected dynamical spacetime obeys the equations of motion for a massive scalar field in an analogue spacetime. even with backreaction, the analogue metric has the same form as that without backreaction, except that the sound velocity, fluid density, and fluid velocity incorporate small corrections that account for backreaction. moreover, the modification of the classical fluid-dynamical equations by backreaction introduces a spacetime-dependent mass. we also present a linear form of the modified bogoliubov-de gennes equation with number conservation, which allows us to solve it numerically. using a finite-size homogeneous quasi-one-dimensional bose gas as an example, we find that backreaction enhances the canonically normal-ordered correlation function at the same point, by about $10\%$ in the bulk and up to about $20\%$ near the edges. the bulk enhancement persists when the finite imaging resolution of cold-atom experiments is taken into account.

title: matching tidal deformability (wilson) coefficients to black hole love numbers in higher-curvature gravity
abstract: we present a consistent mapping between tidal deformability coefficients (tidal love numbers) and wilson coefficients in effective field theory (eft) descriptions of higher-curvature theories of gravity. in this work, we focus on the connection between the static response of a non-spinning black hole and the corresponding wilson coefficient governing tidal imprints in gravitational-wave signals. we analyze a set of control cases to identify the key ingredients required for a systematic computation and matching procedure. in doing so, we highlight shortcomings in existing results that rely on the standard matching approach used in general relativity when applied to higher-curvature gravity theories. as an explicit demonstration, we compute the relevant coefficients for cubic gravity theories. our findings bridge an important gap in the correspondence between tidal love numbers and wilson coefficients in eft extensions of general relativity, which had not been thoroughly explored previously.

title: novel ringdown tests of general relativity with black hole graybody factors
abstract: we present greyring, a new model for the post-merger signal in black-hole binary coalescences based on the graybody factor of the remnant. the model accurately reproduces the full frequency-domain ringdown signal of a large set of comparable-mass, aligned-spin numerical relativity waveforms, achieving mismatches of order ${\cal o}(10^{-6})$ for the dominant $(\ell,m)=(2,2)$ mode, and typically outperforming state-of-the-art time-domain models. building on this model, we introduce a novel consistency test of strong gravity based on the graybody factor: the remnant mass and spin inferred from greyring can be compared with those obtained through standard black hole spectroscopy. this agnostic test relies exclusively on the post-merger signal and does not require the inclusion of overtones or the choice of very early ringdown starting times, combining the advantages of inspiral-merger-ringdown consistency tests and traditional black hole spectroscopy. we apply the test to gw250114 and find that the remnant mass and spin inferred from greyring are consistent with those measured from the full signal. remarkably, the inferred parameters can be measured with a precision comparable to, or slightly better than, that achieved with standard black-hole spectroscopy. our graybody-factor waveform model allows for new precision tests of strong gravity using the ringdown signal.

title: gravitational properties of the monopole bag
abstract: axionic cosmologies constitute a class of models with phenomenologically rich symmetry breaking in the early universe. in the case where monopoles are present in such a background, the axion profile may be deformed; it is possible to construct a ``monopole bag" state composed of a central monopole within a closed axion domain wall. we consider the gravitational properties of this composite defect, and propose that there exist both a horizonless and a black hole-like static solution for different input parameters. for the latter case, we present our results as a first step towards a new construction of a dyonic regular black hole, given the monopole bag's potential ability to evade the usual singular gravitational collapse and retain a non-trivial axionic profile by the exotic electromagnetic properties of an axionic chern-simons term.

title: binary black hole coalescence and the dynamics of scalar hair in einstein-maxwell-scalar theory
abstract: we investigate the head-on coalescence of charged binary black holes in einstein-maxwell-scalar (ems) theory using numerical relativity. the binaries are built from charged puncture initial data representing two reissner-nordström black holes immersed in a purely kinetic scalar perturbation: the scalar field initially vanishes, while its conjugate momentum provides a small seed for the instability. we evolve the coupled gravitational, electromagnetic, and scalar sectors and monitor the apparent horizons, the emitted radiation, and the scalar field on the horizons. our simulations show that the nonminimal electromagnetic-scalar coupling can dynamically trigger the growth of scalar hair even when the individual black holes are initially scalar-free. the subsequent evolution depends on the coupling parameter $α_0$ and on the charge-to-mass ratio of the remnant. for weak coupling, or when charge cancellation suppresses the electromagnetic source after the merger, the scalar field is radiated away or absorbed by the final horizon, and the system dynamically descalarizes. for sufficiently strong coupling and nonzero remnant charge, the scalar field remains finite, and the final black hole approaches a scalarized configuration. for binaries with equal charge-to-mass ratios, $q_1=q_2=0.1$, our simulations identify a transition region between $1900<α_0<2000$, that separates descalarized and scalarized remnants. the coalescence also excites scalar radiation whose time profile is qualitatively correlated with the dominant gravitational-wave mode during the nonlinear stage of the collision. these results provide a binary realization of scalarization/descalarization transitions in ems theory and show that the fate of scalar hair is controlled by the interplay between the scalar coupling and the charge content of the remnant.

title: memoirs of the curvaton: non-perturbative non-gaussianity and supermassive primordial black holes
abstract: the curvaton provides a simple mechanism for generating strongly non-gaussian curvature perturbations after inflation, with potentially important consequences on small scales. we study curvaton dynamics beyond the standard quadratic potential and construct the local non-gaussian map $ζ=f(ζ_{\rm g})$ relating the curvature perturbation to an auxiliary gaussian field $ζ_{\rm g}$. curvaton self-interactions make the onset of oscillations field dependent and modify the effective equation of state once the curvaton enters the adiabatic regime. we incorporate these effects using the abbreviated action, which provides a compact way to connect the frozen and oscillatory regimes and exposes sources of non-gaussianity absent in the purely quadratic case. we apply the formalism to quadratic, monomial, quartic, and cosine potentials, for which we derive the mapping $f(ζ_{\rm g})$ and show that self-interactions can either enhance or suppress the resulting non-gaussianity depending on the potential and initial conditions. we consider non-perturbative aspects in the strongly non-gaussian regime, and show how strong non-gaussianity can suppress the power spectrum. as an application, we provide a bottom-up scenario in which strongly positive curvaton non-gaussianity allows primordial supermassive black hole seeds at peak amplitudes $\mathcal{a}_{\rm pk}\sim10^{-5}$, which are compatible with the cobe/firas $μ$-distortion bounds. this opens a new primordial scenario for the little red dots observed by the jwst. the axion-like curvaton provides a particularly natural setting for this mechanism.

title: gravitational lensing by extremal rotating black holes in the strong deflection limit
abstract: in the strong deflection regime, light rays passing close to an astrophysical black hole may remain trapped near unstable photon orbits for a long time before escaping to infinity. the traditional strong-deflection limit, which accurately describes the logarithmic divergence of the deflection angle for spherically symmetric and slowly rotating black holes, breaks down when the relevant prograde critical photon orbit coincides with the degenerate horizon of an extremal rotating black hole. we present a new strong deflection limit expansion for this horizon critical orbit, covering a general class of extremal rotating black holes. we show that the deflection angle exhibits a stronger power-law divergence in addition to the logarithmic divergence. for an adequate description of higher-order images, additional terms in the expansion must be retained. we first study prograde gravitational lensing in the equatorial plane and then extend the analysis to quasi-equatorial motion, which allows us to calculate the magnification of the higher-order images and the position of the caustic points. we finally apply the general framework to explicit examples, including the kerr, kerr-newman, and kerr-sen metrics.

title: exploring exact einsteinian black hole physics in dark matter environment: ray tracing, stability, eikonal qnms and thermodynamics
abstract: motivated by the recent rebuttal of black hole--dark matter solutions based on velocity-matching, we reconstruct the spacetime by treating the dark matter halo density directly as an energy-density source in the einstein field equations. we obtain an exact static, spherically symmetric black hole solution and investigate the effects of the halo on its geometry, optical properties, quasinormal modes, and thermodynamics. using null geodesics, we show that the halo modifies photon trajectories, shifts the circular photon orbit, and enlarges the photon sphere and apparent shadow. the lyapunov exponent of the unstable null orbit further determines the eikonal quasinormal modes, yielding explicit halo-induced corrections to their oscillation and damping rates. we also compute the mass, hawking temperature, entropy, heat capacity, and gibbs free energy to characterize the thermodynamic stability and phase structure. we find that the dark matter halo enlarges the domain of thermodynamic stability and introduces nontrivial phase behavior absent in the schwarzschild case, demonstrating that astrophysical dark matter environments can leave potentially observable imprints on black hole observables.

title: disformal maps: classification and singular dynamics
abstract: being agnostic about the field content of a gravitational system, we consider a general disformal transformation of the metric, $g_{μν}=c h_{μν}+d t_{μν}$, on a four-dimensional lorentzian manifold. using the cayley-hamilton theorem, we derive an explicit formula for the inverse disformed metric. implementing the hawking-ellis classification, we categorize disformal transformations into four types: type i, ii, iii, and iv, based on possible jordan block structures. we further identify the segre subclasses from the eigenvalues. we derive explicit relations between the cayley-hamilton degree of $t_{μν}$, its hawking-ellis type, and its segre subclass, restricting the possible types from the degree alone. in some cases, the type can be determined without even performing a full jordan decomposition. for singular transformations, when new dynamical degrees of freedom emerge, we obtain the form of their corresponding mimetic energy-momentum tensor $t^\star_{μν}$. within the polynomial sector, the hawking-ellis types of $t_{μν}$ and $t^\star_{μν}$ always coincide for type i. for types ii and iii it can differ, while type iv is preserved generically but can reduce to type i when the complex pair is mapped to a repeated real eigenvalue. this makes it possible to infer physical properties of $t^\star_{μν}$ directly from the hawking-ellis type of $t_{μν}$. we apply our setup to scalar and gauge fields. we find a new pure-disformal scalar-gauge family yielding irrotational perfect fluids, including barotropic fluids with an arbitrary constant equation-of-state parameter. two scalar fields realize all four types and the reductions from types ii and iv to type i. this framework applies to the kinematical and dynamical study of invertible and non-invertible disformal transformations with different field content.

title: gravitational lensing outside and inside of a marginally unstable photon sphere at a $z_2$-symmetric wormhole throat in strong deflection limits
abstract: the deflection angles of rays diverge logarithmically near outside and inside of a photon sphere in usual strong deflection limits and the rays near the photon sphere could be detected by near-future space observations on black hole shadows. on the other hand, we show that the deflection angles of the rays near the photon sphere at a throat of a $z_2$-symmetric wormhole, as an example among some commonly used types of wormholes or simple wormholes, which is often studied by the event horizon telescope collaborations, diverge in power law but not logarithmically. this is because the $z_2$-symmetric wormhole has a marginally unstable photon sphere at the throat and it has neither a common nor simple but special property. we investigate gravitational lensing of the rays nearly outside and inside of the marginally unstable photon sphere at the throat in a class of $z_2$-symmetric wormholes in the strong deflection limits. we use a numerical method to calculate the deflection angles diverging in power law and we apply it to the commonly-used simple wormhole spacetime, a damour-solodukhin wormhole spacetime, and a simpson-visser black-bounce spacetime. our numerical results imply universal property of the deflection angle of the rays near the marginally unstable photon sphere on $z_2$-symmetric wormhole throat in the strong deflection limits as similar to the deflection angles of ray bent by a marginally unstable photon sphere off a throat in the strong deflection limits which have a different power. we also correct the coefficients of power-law divergent terms of the deflection angles of the rays bent nearly outside of the marginally unstable photon sphere at the $z_2$-symmetric wormhole throat in a semi-analytic approach investigated by the author and others.

title: boundary-induced corrections to the response of an unruh-dewitt detector outside a compact star with robin surface conditions
abstract: we formulate the finite-time response problem for a radially accelerated unruh--dewitt detector coupled to a real massless scalar field outside a static, spherically symmetric, horizonless compact star. the stellar exterior is described by the schwarzschild geometry, while unresolved field--surface interactions are represented by a local robin condition at the stellar radius. after reducing the klein--gordon equation to a half-line schrödinger problem, we identify a sufficiently stable branch of the robin family from positivity of the radial operator, construct delta-normalized continuum modes, and define the static ground state with respect to schwarzschild time. we derive a mode-amplitude representation of the smoothly switched detector response that avoids a direct numerical treatment of the coincidence singularity of the wightman distribution. we obtain a radially aligned trajectory of constant signed proper acceleration in terms of the rapidity measured by static observers. the resulting formulation separates the effects of compactness, surface condition, closest approach, detector gap, and interaction duration. we also state the flat-space, dirichlet, static-detector, low-frequency, large-distance, and long-interaction limits required to validate a numerical implementation. the framework provides a controlled extension of detector studies with static reflective compact objects to finite-time moving probes.

title: phase transitions and quasinormal modes of euler-heisenberg-dilaton ads black holes
abstract: in this paper, we study phase transitions and scalar quasinormal modes(qnms) of magnetically charged euler--heisenberg-dilaton ads black holes in the extended phase space. we classify the horizon structures for all three signs of the eh coupling and derive the extended first law when the pressure and coupling are varied. for negative coupling, the physical branch exhibits a van der waals-like small/large black-hole transition. using the improved asymptotic iteration method, we find two separated qnm trajectories below the critical pressure, whereas they merge into one continuous curve at the critical point. the ghs limit and the positive couplings considered here do not produce a finite-radius critical point.

title: random wave chaos on momentum-fractionated microstate geometries
abstract: we study the role of momentum fractionation in the development of chaos on smooth 3-charge supergravity solutions of d1-d5 theory, specifically momentum-fractionated superstrata. we probe the chaos through the dynamics of null geodesics and waves. on fractionated backgrounds, both geodesics and waves show uniformly strong chaos (large chaotic sea and near-perfect agreement with the berry random wave hypothesis). in contrast, geodesics and waves on single-mode (non-fractionated) superstrata are closer to separability (although still chaotic). we discuss a possibility that such dichotomy can be related to the expectation that monotone bps states are less chaotic than fortuitous ones. finally, we explain why our chaos probes are meaningful for microstate geometries even though they become trivial in the black hole limit.

title: quasinormal modes of rotating black holes with ultralight scalar fields
abstract: we report the first accurate computation of the leading-order shifts in the quasinormal-mode frequencies of rapidly rotating black holes surrounded by massive scalar fields with nonminimal curvature coupling. for fields with reduced compton wavelengths no shorter than the black-hole mass scale, the numerical errors in the frequency shifts are typically $10^{-8} - 10^{-5}$ for dimensionless spins between 0 and 0.9, and at most $\mathcal{o}(10^{-3})$ next to the scalar-mass threshold. our results open up the possibility of searching for ultralight scalar particles, prime dark-matter candidates, using existing gravitational-wave signals.

title: spiral galaxy spacetime in extended scalar-tensor-gauss-bonnet gravity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics
abstract: in this work, using nonlinear electrodynamics (nled) as a source in the field equations of extended scalar-tensor-gauss-bonnet (e-stgb) gravity, a novel type of static and spherically symmetric spacetime is found. we show that this novel type of spacetime can be used to explain the rotation curves and gravitational lensing of spiral galaxies. the nled model used to derive our solution, in the weak and strong field limits, reduces to maxwell electrodynamics. furthermore, for a wide range of parameter values where our solution describes the gravitational field of a spiral galaxy, the nled model satisfies the null and weak energy conditions. hence, our results suggest that the extended scalar-tensor-gauss-bonnet gravity minimally coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics (e-stgb-nled) provides a viable alternative to explain flat rotation curves of spiral galaxies without invoking dark matter.

title: retarded green function for bopp--podolsky electrodynamics in four-dimensional de sitter spacetime
abstract: we study classical bopp--podolsky (bp) electrodynamics on four-dimensional de sitter spacetime, focusing on its transverse retarded green function and gauge-invariant electromagnetic response. because de sitter spacetime is maximally symmetric, its vector green functions admit a covariant expansion in a finite basis of invariant bitensors, with scalar coefficients depending only on the invariant separation. for conserved sources, the fourth-order field operator factorizes into maxwell and massive-vector operators, yielding the bp retarded kernel as the difference of their transverse green functions. using the invariant bitensor decomposition, we reduce the propagator equations to a hypergeometric master equation and determine the distributional structure of its solution. the common leading short-distance singularity of the maxwell and massive-vector sectors cancels, leaving a logarithmic master singularity and a softened vector-potential wavefront. after one curl, the gauge-invariant field-strength kernel contains a null-cone delta distribution and a regular timelike tail. the smooth maxwell master tail is annihilated by the curl, so the interior electromagnetic tail is generated entirely by the massive sector. we also derive an exact horizon-regular static potential, demonstrate the cancellation of the coulomb divergence, recover the flat-space bp potential, and formulate the generalized gauss law. on global de sitter spacetime, the compactness of the spatial sections requires the total charge to vanish; we implement this constraint using an antipodal charge configuration with smooth factorized initial data. the analysis is classical and does not assume a quantum lee--wick contour or a preferred de sitter vacuum.

title: charge-activated birefringence of an einstein-tensor-coupled vector field on reissner--nordström black holes
abstract: we study the propagation of a neutral vector test field non-minimally coupled to the einstein tensor on a reissner--nordström black hole. the interaction vanishes on a vacuum background, so electric charge is required to activate the curvature-induced response. the parity potentials have one symmetry: reversing the sign of the coupling exchanges the electric and magnetic susceptibilities. because of this symmetry, the two polarizations respond identically at first order in the coupling. the dominant propagation-level effect is therefore a common shift of the effective photon sphere and of the shadow radius, not a birefringent splitting. the variation of shadow size can mimic the charge variation of a black hole. when the coupling is weak, polarization splitting appears only in the second-order term, distinguishing this interaction from corrections involving only charge. we follow this ordering through full-frequency absorption and scattering, the semiclassical glory, and ray-traced double shadows. the absorption parity asymmetry and the shadow rim splitting probe the difference between the effective potentials. the polarization-summed backward scattering isolates the helicity-reversing response, which is zero without the coupling. at the positive-coupling boundary the splitting grows but stays finite. beyond it the even-parity potential has a pole outside the horizon. in the high-multipole limit, the two boundaries of the stability window both correspond to the thresholds of bound-state instability, but their physical properties differ: the negatively coupled boundary forms a regular potential well, while the positively coupled boundary marks the breaking of regularity. a frobenius analysis shows a forced logarithmic branch at that pole. without an additional physical connection condition, the continuation across the pole is not unique.

title: hamiltonian surface charges in general parallel relativity
abstract: general parallel relativity is a dynamically equivalent formulation of einstein gravity in which the parallel frame supplies explicit boundary reference data. in this formulation, finite-region energy-momentum and horizon entropy arise as distinct hamiltonian surface charges. diffeomorphisms along canonical frame directions define a quasi-local energy-momentum including a matter surface term, while normal-plane boosts at a smooth horizon give entropy. these covariant formulas are applied to the reissner-nordström black hole and to a dilatonic charged black hole. in both examples, the matter contribution and its legendre transform complete the misner-sharp mass into the hamiltonian energy appropriate to the chosen electromagnetic boundary datum. the resulting horizon charges satisfy the thermodynamic relation obtained independently from the euclidean boundary action.

title: metric and dilaton information from high-overtone quasinormal modes of analytic einstein-maxwell-dilaton black holes
abstract: black-hole interiors are hidden from exterior observers, yet their geometry can enter the high-overtone spectrum of linear perturbations. we study how this spectrum encodes metric and supporting-matter information in analytic einstein--maxwell--dilaton black holes. coupling a neutral spectator to the dilaton at fixed uv dimension provides a matter-sensitive channel alongside the momentum response. for real-endpoint spacelike connections, the momentum response and mass-label dependence separate the metric exponents from the signed dilaton slope. near the causal threshold, a complex endpoint controls the spectral family: the mass profiles approach a common value, producing a shared fractional correction, while regular propagation retains label dependence. this mechanism is present at criticality without an inner horizon and continues locally into timelike interiors. exterior numerical spectra support the reconstruction and the leading complex-endpoint responses. local scaling and probe coupling set the candidate responses, while wave connection determines their imprint on the exterior spectrum.

title: quasibound states of charged dirac fields around einstein-euler-heisenberg black holes
abstract: we study quasibound states of a massive charged dirac field on the einstein--euler--heisenberg (eeh) black hole, the extension of reissner--nordström (rn) by the leading weak-field vacuum-polarization term of qed. we derive the background to first order in the euler--heisenberg coupling $a$. we show that it admits a nondegenerate horizon at $q=m$ and an extremal charge $q_{\rm ext}=m[1+a/(40m^2)+\mathcal{o}(a^2)]>m$, with horizon data that depend on $\sqrt a$ near extremality. from the separated radial equations, we derive an identity that excludes real-frequency quasibound states on any background of this class, so damped branches cannot become unstable. since the eeh corrections first enter at $\mathcal{o}(r^{-5})$ in the electrostatic potential, the trapping condition $mμ^2-qqω_r>0$ and the hydrogenic spectrum coincide with rn, and no fine-structure-order splitting arises. two-sided shooting with a muller root finder shows that the real frequencies shift only by near-zone amounts that are linear in $a$ and strongly suppressed with angular momentum. the damping rates respond in a branch-dependent way. at $q/m=0.99$ the $\ell=0$ ground state becomes slightly longer-lived, while the $(n_r,j,\ell,λ)=(0,\tfrac32,1,-2)$ state decays up to $80\%$ faster for $a/m^2\le1$, and near the trapping threshold the damping rate increases by up to $60\%$. switching on the metric and potential corrections separately, together with a wkb analysis of the inner barrier, identifies the mechanisms: coulomb screening always increases leakage, while the metric correction controls the sign and size of the $\ell$-dependent effect. characteristic time-domain evolutions with richardson-extrapolated matrix-pencil extraction reproduce the frequency-domain shifts.

title: bartnik's splitting conjecture and the cosmological wall: a cauchy busemann function approach
abstract: bartnik's conjecture states that a timelike geodesically complete cosmological spacetime satisfying the timelike convergence condition splits as a static product. we show that any counterexample exhibits a peculiar global causal structure: two disjoint open regions, the future and the past cosmological developments, separated by a non-empty closed causally convex set: the cosmological wall. the developments are bounded by $c^0$ null hypersurfaces, the cosmological horizons, and a component of each horizon contains a lightlike line. these objects are natural and hence carry physical significance, as they do not depend on the choice of cauchy hypersurface. they can be defined through the cauchy busemann functions $b^\pm$ of a compact cauchy hypersurface $σ$, the developments being their finiteness domains. using a product trick we show that $b^+$ is the graph function of a cauchy horizon in $m\times \mathbb{r}$, and so inherits the regularity and dynamical properties of horizons: $b^+$ is continuous, locally lipschitz and locally semi-concave on its finiteness domain, and its calibrated curves are timelike rays. we prove that if the two cosmological developments intersect, which happens whenever $b^+$ is $c^1$ on its finiteness domain, then the spacetime contains a timelike line and hence splits, a result which recovers several positive results of the literature. we also obtain a localized rigidity version of hawking's singularity theorem: if some compact cauchy hypersurface has non-positive mean curvature on the future development, the spacetime splits. hence, in a counterexample, every compact cauchy hypersurface expands somewhere in the future development and contracts somewhere in the past one. if the wall has empty interior, it coincides with both horizons and is ruled by lightlike lines, and under null completeness its components are smooth totally geodesic null hypersurfaces.

title: vanishing love numbers of kerr-newman black holes
abstract: tidal love numbers characterize the conservative response of compact objects to external perturbations and provide a powerful probe of their nature. while the static love numbers of schwarzschild, kerr, and reissner--nordström black holes remarkably vanish, the tidal response of a generic kerr--newman black hole has remained unexplored due to the intrinsic coupling between gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations. exploiting a recent breakthrough in the separability of these perturbations, we analytically determine the static tidal response of the most general stationary black hole in four-dimensional einstein--maxwell theory. for arbitrary multipole order, charge, and spin, we show that the entire matrix of conservative love numbers vanishes, including the mixed gravito-electromagnetic couplings. we also compute the nonvanishing static dissipative response induced by frame dragging.

title: mri turbulence versus $α$-viscosity in circumbinary disks: implications for gravitational-wave dephasing and accretion variability
