abstract: our understanding of gas torques on massive black hole binaries (mbhbs) relies on hydrodynamical (hd) simulations of circumbinary disks (cbds) in which an $α$-viscosity models angular momentum transport. however, cbds around mbhbs near merger are hot, magnetized plasmas where transport is driven by magnetohydrodynamical (mhd) turbulence sustained by the magnetorotational instability (mri). we test how well an $α$-viscosity captures mri turbulence with 3d global athena++ simulations of a locally isothermal cbd around an equal-mass, circular mbhb, run in hd and mhd from the same initial torus on identical grids, so that only the transport mechanism differs. excising the region within twice the binary separation, $r<2~a_{\rm bin}$, allows $1000$ orbits of evolution, several times longer than previous mhd simulations. both disks deliver the same accretion rate, and the gas beyond $2~a_{\rm bin}$ exerts a positive torque in both, yet the mhd torque is $3.5$ times larger and $3$ times more variable. near the midplane, transport is similar in the disk body but three times weaker in mhd at the cavity edge, where $2$-$3$ times more mass piles up in a more eccentric cavity, raising the torque. the accretion rate is modulated mainly at twice the binary frequency in hd, but by a persistent lump at the cavity edge and its beat with the binary in mhd. the outer-disk torque therefore implies a contribution to the gas-induced phase shift in the gravitational-wave signal of lisa binaries $3.5$ times larger than in $α$-disk models, and a different variability signature for lsst and roman.

title: null-energy bounds on photon-orbit instability in einstein-gauss-bonnet gravity
abstract: we derive a local upper bound on the coordinate-time lyapunov exponent of unstable circular null orbits in static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat einstein--gauss--bonnet gravity in $n\geq5$ dimensions with nonnegative gauss--bonnet coupling. on the regular einstein branch, the tangential null energy condition suffices; no additional density-pressure inequality is required for the principal result. the bound retains the local matter-density contribution dictated by the field equations. using the spherical mass relation, we express the departure of its dimensionless coefficient from the einstein value $n-3$ in terms of the difference between the local density and the enclosed generalized misner--sharp mass per areal volume. this gives a sufficient density-contrast criterion for the einstein optical bound to remain valid at nonzero coupling. optical gaussian curvature and tangential null convergence provide geometrical interpretations that distinguish radial tidal instability from the focusing of a null congruence. vacuum solutions saturate the bound, while a maxwell field with nonzero charge produces a strictly positive gap. the smooth einstein limit and explicit vacuum and charged solutions provide consistency checks. a separate matter condition yields a density-free corollary. we also discuss consequences for strong-deflection lensing and test-field eikonal damping within their respective regimes of validity.

title: einstein telescope: the triangle in a network and the impact of the relative orientation of detectors
abstract: the geometrical configuration of the einstein telescope (et) gravitational-wave observatory is one the most important design choices to be made for this future scientific facility. two baseline configurations are currently being considered, a single triangle or 2 distant l-shaped detectors tilted by about $45^{\circ}$. in this document we present a study of the scientific performance of the et baseline configurations in both stand-alone mode and in the presence of either an l-shaped cosmic explorer detector with 40-km long arms located in the united states or the existing ligo-virgo-kagra network. we also include in the study an alternative et configuration, which is currently not being considered and consists of a triangle plus a distant l-shaped detector. we find that in stand-alone mode this alternative configuration performs significantly better than the other two in both the compact binary coalescence and stochastic gravitational wave background scientific cases. the differences in performance between the et configurations are reduced in the presence of the considered, additional non-et detectors. we also show that the impact of possible correlated noise in co-located detectors on the stochastic gravitational-wave background performance can be addressed with the addition of extra detectors. finally, we study the impact on the et scientific performance of the relative orientation of the future detectors in the network. we find that, while the configurations that include a triangular et detector are basically insensitive to this orientation, a balanced compromise for the et configuration consisting of two l-shaped detectors could be represented by a tilt angle between the two detectors of about $30^{\circ}$.

title: mathematical framework for simulation of non-perturbative cavity optomechanics with plate-like dielectrics
abstract: cavity optomechanical models typically treat a sensor either as a perturbative polarizable object in a pre-existing optical field, or solve the field at a fixed equilibrium and linearize in a fixed optical-mode basis. neither self-consistently determines the spatially resolved cavity field, the optical force, the mechanical equilibrium, and the back-action when a finite-thickness dielectric plate intercepts the entire optical mode and restructures the intracavity field. in this companion paper to [1], we develop that treatment by extending the vacuum two-photon formalism to finite-thickness planar dielectrics, incorporating their fresnel reflection, internal propagation, optical forces, and mechanical back-action directly into the field equations. we derive the carrier and sideband transfer functions needed to describe the coupled optical-mechanical system, including optomechanical cooling and the response to external perturbations. the result is a systematic starting point for calculating detector response and noise budgets for cavity experiments with intracavity dielectrics, including gravitational wave detectors deploying levitated sensors.

title: black holes with dark matter halos and a positive cosmological constant: energy conditions and signatures
abstract: we study static, spherically symmetric black holes surrounded by dark matter halos in the presence of a positive cosmological constant. assuming vanishing radial pressure, we derive the constraints imposed by the null, weak, strong, and dominant energy conditions on the halo matter. the halo is confined to a finite radial interval separated from both horizons, and the total mass is bounded above by the nariai value. we construct a hernquist-type profile and study black hole images, showing that a positive cosmological constant can substantially change the images. we also compute scalar quasinormal modes of the hernquist-type spacetime. when the dark matter mass is sufficiently small, the relative difference of a selected mode is approximately linear in the compactness of the matter halo, i.e., the ratio of mass parameter $m_{\text{dm}}$ and scale parameter $a$, with a coefficient that depends on the cosmological constant.

title: exact radial stability threshold for a minkowski-schwarzschild thin shell
abstract: we study the stability of a thin shell of ordinary matter that separates a flat interior from a schwarzschild exterior, which is the simplest model of a subluminal warp drive. the matter content of the shell is fixed by the junction conditions and satisfies all the standard energy conditions except very close to the horizon. for a shell made of causal matter we find an exact radius below which it cannot be stable under radial perturbations. we then place a black hole inside the shell and show that this radius grows with the black hole mass, so that the flat interior is the most favourable case. since such shells are known to be unstable to non-radial perturbations, our result marks the boundary of the region in which any stabilising mechanism would have to operate.

title: quasiperiodic oscillations as probes of rotating black holes in exponential dark matter environments
abstract: we construct the rotating counterpart of a black hole embedded in a dark-matter halo with the exponential-sphere profile $ρ=ρ_0e^{-r/r_0}$, using the newman--janis algorithm in the azreg-a\"ınou form, and study its imprints on test-particle motion and quasiperiodic oscillations (qpos). we derive closed-form orbital and epicyclic frequencies valid for any kerr-like metric with a mass function and show that, to first order, the halo enters them only through its central density, acting as an effective cosmological constant $λ_{eff}=8πρ_0$; the corrections are therefore universal for all cored profiles. the halo moves the innermost stable circular orbit outward and produces an outer boundary of stable orbits, while the sign of the frequency shift depends on the assumed equation of state of the halo. fitting the relativistic precession model to the simultaneous qpo triplets of gro~j1655$-$40 and xte~j1859+226 with markov-chain monte carlo sampling yields spins and emission radii consistent with kerr and $ρ_0m^2<2.9\times10^{-5}$ and $3.0\times10^{-5}$ (95\%), respectively. in physical units these limits exclude only ultra-dense dark cores, $ρ_0\gtrsim10^{11}$~g\,cm$^{-3}$.

title: adiabatic particle production in a time-dependent accelerated frame
abstract: we study a massive scalar field in flat spacetime written in a time-dependent accelerated frame whose fixed-coordinate observers have maximal proper acceleration at $t=0$ and become asymptotically inertial without forming a horizon. the klein-gordon equation separates into a modified mathieu equation in time and a confining schrödinger problem in space with a discrete spectrum. we impose an adiabatic vacuum at the instant of maximal acceleration and compute the particle number in the inertial future. for the zeroth-order adiabatic state it falls as the inverse eighth power of the initial mode frequency, and raising the adiabatic order cancels successive terms of the endpoint expansion, in analogy with the switching transients of finite-time detectors. analytic continuation of the spatial eigenfunctions gives the out modes in closed form and an exact expression for the particle number, which is entirely the mismatch at $t=0$ between the initial state and the out vacuum. the spectrum is algebraic rather than planckian.

title: dirac stars in modified $f(r)$ gravity
abstract: we study dirac mini-stars in modified $r^2$ gravity, where gravity is sourced by both linear and nonlinear spinor fields. two-dimensional (2d) and three-dimensional (3d) profiles of the mini-star mass are constructed as functions of the spinor frequency (for the 2d profiles) and the central value of the spinor field (for the 3d profiles) in general relativity and modified gravity for various values of the spinor nonlinearity parameter. we show that the modification of gravity alters the properties of these configurations, while increasing the nonlinearity parameter within the framework of $r^2$ gravity significantly changes the profiles of the spinor and metric functions, the effective energy density, and the dependence of the total mass on the oscillation frequency. the most pronounced changes occur at large values of the nonlinearity parameter.

title: on the mathematical foundations of gravitational decoupling in general relativity
abstract: we study the algebraic and geometric structures of gravitational decoupling within a fixed class of globally static, spherically symmetric spacetimes with non-vanishing areal-radius differential. we show that (minimal and extended) geometric deformations of the seed metric define a groupoid of partial transformations. we also draw a connection between the geometric deformation procedures and disformal transformations. it is shown that every admissible minimal geometric deformation admits a disformal representation using the areal radius as an auxiliary scalar. for extended deformations, we derive a necessary condition and exhibit a global obstruction that persists under diffeomorphisms preserving the areal radius and the static killing direction up to constant normalization. finally, we verify that the disformal construction reproduces the standard minimal geometric deformation source equations and separate conservation law, including anisotropic seeds.

title: tidal excitation of relativistic stars
abstract: how a relativistic star responds to a time-dependent tide has lacked a first-principles counterpart of the newtonian normal-mode expansion. in general relativity, the tidal field is gauge sensitive, radiative modes are non-hermitian and incomplete, and the direct and late-time responses are intrinsically nonmodal. in this work we present, to our knowledge, the first causal relativistic theory that treats all of these components on equal footing. we first develop the spectral decomposition of the retarded green function of the matched stellar interior--schwarzschild exterior, which classifies four separate regimes in time domain: acausal region, prompt wave, surface-reflected wave, and mode+tail. the prompt signal is identical to that of a schwarzschild black hole with the same mass, which is combined with the surface-reflected wave to be referred as the "direct part". with the green function and a complex bilinear form on the full metric--fluid phase space, we decompose the linear response of a nonrotating perfect-fluid star into direct, quasinormal-mode, and late-time-tail sectors. crucially, every sector admits an explicit first-order driven evolution equation: discrete bilinear projections determine the dynamically evolving quasinormal-mode amplitudes, while continuum projections of the same tidal source onto branch-cut states determine the direct and tail amplitudes. the result is a complete modal--nonmodal decomposition of the spacetime and fluid perturbations, which is physically described by the dynamics of a discrete and a continuous-frequency set of oscillators. we verify the decomposition numerically under generic time-dependent tidal driving and discuss applications to black hole perturbations.

title: linear response to black hole deformations
abstract: modifications of gravity beyond (vacuum) general relativity have a subtle impact on the physics around black holes. describing these effects across different observables is, however, a priori strongly model dependent. while effective descriptions of the geometry allow to efficiently capture deviations from benchmark predictions, they sometimes lack a clear passage towards (effective) new physics. inspired by linear response theory, in this work i therefore propose a formalism that allows to calculate leading corrections of observables relative to the schwarzschild black hole anywhere in space-time (outside of the horizon): the order of corrections is fixed through an eigenvalue $\mathcal{e}$ of the einstein tensor, which is identified with an external energy momentum tensor that generates the deformation of the geometry. in this ways, $\mathcal{e}$ can be linked to effective physics models. focusing on spherically symmetric and static black holes, i illustrate the approach at the hand of a number of observables in the vicinity of the horizon, such as characteristic quantities of particles moving around the black hole (e.g. the black hole shadow or the radius of the innermost stable circular orbit) or the spectrum of scalar quasi-normal modes. reversing the logic, i argue that the knowledge of such observables provides non-trivial constraints on $\mathcal{e}$, which in turn grant insights into the effective physics in the vicinity of the black hole.

title: testing compact binary nature in eccentric orbits with third-generation detectors
abstract: the spin-induced quadrupole moment (siqm) of a compact object provides a direct null test of the kerr hypothesis. most existing gravitational-wave tests of siqm assume quasi-circular binaries, although dynamical formation channels can produce measurable eccentricity that may persist in the sensitive band of third-generation (3g) detectors. we extend the symmetric siqm test to eccentric, aligned-spin binaries using a post-newtonian spinning-eccentric phasing model, and forecast its measurability with cosmic explorer (ce) and einstein telescope (et). single-event fisher-matrix forecasts show that the impact of eccentricity on siqm measurement precision depends on the binary parameters and detector configuration, rather than uniformly degrading the measurement. a population study with a truncated eccentric expansion indicates that et's additional low-frequency eccentric cycles tighten $δκ_s$ by roughly a factor of two relative to ce (median $0.11$ to $0.12$ versus $0.20$ to $0.23$); the absolute values are indicative only. we further show that quasi-circular template banks can lose significant effectualness for moderately eccentric signals, motivating the development of eccentric-spin template families. accounting for eccentricity is therefore important both for siqm measurements and for avoiding systematic losses in searches, and it strengthens tests of the nature of compact objects with 3g gravitational-wave detectors.

title: a scale-critical $μ<\frac38$ extension principle for spherically symmetric einstein-scalar field system
abstract: we present a new quantitative, scale-critical $c^1$ extension principle for the spherically symmetric einstein--scalar field system. we derive estimates for solutions in the causal past of a possibly singular endpoint $\mathcal{o}$ of the center. assume that there is no trapped surface in this region and assume that the doppler exponent (blue shift) along each incoming null cone is uniformly bounded. we then prove that the solution can extend regularly across $\mathcal{o}$ provided the mass ratio $μ=2m/r$ satisfies $\supμ<\frac38$. this improves the small-mass-ratio condition in christodoulou's extension principle by an explicit threshold of order one. our proof has three new ingredients. first, we derive several new uniform scale-critical pointwise estimates for the scalar field and its derivatives. second, we obtain refined estimates in an exterior self-similar domain within the triangular causal past region. third, we establish a family of higher-order morawetz-type identities and identify the ranges of $μ$, with which there are coercive spacetime estimates. the unweighted identity yields the threshold $μ\leq\frac14$, while employing extra self-similar weight raises the threshold to $μ<\frac38$ and provides a weighted control, which implies that the solution's bv norm along an outgoing null cone is small, so that christodoulou's theory of bounded variation solutions gives the extension.

title: an extension principle for einstein-maxwell-charged scalar field system with finite doppler exponent
abstract: we prove a new extension principle for the spherically symmetric einstein--maxwell--charged scalar field system. rather than imposing conditions for mass ratio $2m/r$ as in christodoulou's small-mass-ratio criterion or as in an--chen--singh's proof [1] with $2m/r<3/8$, here we work through a proposal by an-tan [2] with finite doppler exponent (blueshift). by conducting two successive blow-up analyses, followed by a stationary comparison and a rigidity argument, we establish the uniform boundness of $α'$ with $α'=\partial_vα/\partial_vr$ and $α=\partial_v(rϕ)/\partial_vr$. this provides the desired extension principle in an-tan [2] and completes the picture of weak cosmic censorship developed therein.   as we were about to release our preprint, cicortas communicated to us that together with his collaborators, they concomitantly used a different approach to obtain the corresponding extension principle with finite blueshift (doppler exponent) for the uncharged einstein-scalar field system. hence, we decided to put the current paper as an appendix to an-tan [2], thereby completing the proof of the weak cosmic censorship for the einstein-maxwell-charged scalar field system. at the same time, we are working with cicortas and his collaborators to write a new preprint containing both approaches for the einstein-scalar field system.

title: separation of variables for coupled radiative perturbations of kerr-newman-de sitter black holes
abstract: we extend hintz's separation of variables for radiative gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations from kerr-newman to kerr-newman-de sitter black holes. on subextremal backgrounds with nonzero rotation and charge, an explicit algebraic matrix transformation yields coupled two-component radial and angular ordinary differential systems linked by a common separation constant. the transformation is independent of the frequency and azimuthal number and applies to both signs of spin weight. for real frequencies, we establish a complete angular mode decomposition. we also translate regularity at the future black hole outer and cosmological horizons into ingoing and outgoing boundary conditions, respectively, for the separated radial systems. these results show that exact separation of the coupled radiative equations extends beyond asymptotically flat kerr-newman spacetime.

title: well- and ill-posedness of the cauchy problem for semi-linear schrödinger equations on the torus
abstract: we consider the cauchy problem for semi-linear schrödinger equations on the torus $\mathbb t$. we establish a necessary and sufficient condition on the polynomial nonlinearity for the cauchy problem to be well-posed in the sobolev space $h^s(\mathbb t)$ for $s>\frac 52$. for the well-posedness, we use the energy estimates and the gauge transformation. for the ill-posedness, we prove the non-existence of solutions to the cauchy problem.

title: on the spectrum of schrödinger operators interacting at two distinct scales
abstract: schrödinger operators of the form $δ- w$ on $l^2_{\text{rad}}(\mathbb{r}^3)$, the space of radially symmetric square integrable functions, are relevant in a variety of physical contexts. the potential $w$ is taken to be radially symmetric (i.e. $w(x) = w(|x|)$) and to decompose into two components with distinct spatial scales: $w=w_\varepsilon:= v_0+v_{1,\varepsilon}$. the second component $v_{1,\varepsilon}(|x|) = \varepsilon^2v_1(\varepsilon |x|)$ represents a scaled potential that becomes increasingly delocalized as $\varepsilon \to 0$. we will assume that both potentials $v_0(r), v_1(r)$ exhibit certain decay properties as $r \to \infty$. we show how the eigenvalue count on the positive real axis is built out of the spectra associated with the two reduced eigenvalue problems on their separate scales. the result is that the total number of eigenvalues of $δ- w$ is the sum of the number of positive eigenvalues of $δ- v_0$ and $δ- v_1$. our analysis combines dynamical systems techniques with a separation of scales argument, providing a novel framework for studying spectral properties of differential operators where multiple spatial scales interact.

title: fractional hypocoercivity in bounded domains in the anomalous diffusion limit
abstract: in this paper, we provide quantitative stability results for several dissipative linear kinetic equations with heavy-tailed equilibria in different geometries. moreover, the approach, inspired by the so-called $l^2$-hypocoercivity method, is robust enough to provide estimates that are uniform in the anomalous diffusion limit. it applies to bounded domains with either periodic or general maxwell boundary conditions (ranging from the pure specular to the pure diffusive case) as well as to the whole-space case. in addition, our framework accommodates linear collisional operators whose coefficients depend on the position.

title: finite-time blow-up for the geng--xue system with an application to the three-component degasperis--procesi system
abstract: we prove finite-time blow-up for the geng--xue system with initial data satisfying $u_0\in w^{p,q}(\r)$ and $n_0\in l^{r'}(\r)$ at sobolev regularity $s\geq2$, where $n=v-v_{xx}$. a cancellation in the balance law for $nu_x$ yields closed convolution estimates that do not depend on an a priori uniform bound for $u_x$. these estimates control $v$ along a characteristic and give an explicit condition on the initial slope, together with an upper bound on the lifespan. the proof does not use conservation laws. for the three-component degasperis--procesi system, the same argument applies to $nu_x+ρ^2-\barρ^2$, where $\barρ\in[0,1]$ is a constant density background. we also prove local well-posedness for this system in $h^{s-1}(\r)\times h^s(\r)\times h^s(\r)$ for $s>\frac32$, and a blow-up criterion in $b^1_{2,1}(\r)\times b^2_{2,1}(\r)\times b^2_{2,1}(\r)$.

title: modified scattering for semiclassical bose-fermi mixtures
abstract: the vlasov-hartree system models a mixture of bosons and fermions interacting via coulomb forces in which the bosons are described quantum-mechanically, while the fermions are described classically. for small initial data, we prove that the system exhibits modified scattering, i.e. the bosonic and fermionic subsystems each converge to solutions of the free schrödinger and vlasov equations respectively, but with coupled logarithmic corrections owing to the long-range nature of coulomb interactions. we use a mixed lagrangian and fourier-based approach to derive explicit descriptions of the asymptotic dynamics of the solution and associated fields and lagrangian trajectories. notably, due to our purely lagrangian analysis on the vlasov side, we require no derivatives on the initial fermion density, the asymptotic fermionic profile is as regular as the initial data, and convergence occurs in almost the same space as the initial data.

title: nondegeneracy and asymptotic behavior of type i blow-up for semilinear heat equations with general nonlinearities
abstract: we study the local asymptotic behavior of nonnegative type i blow-up solutions to semilinear heat equations with nonlinearities that need not be scale invariant. using a quasi-similarity transformation adapted to the associated ordinary differential equation, we establish locally uniform convergence to a constant profile on the parabolic spatial scale near every interior blow-up point. under a quantitative assumption on the nonlinearity at infinity, our results cover regularly varying nonlinearities in the sobolev subcritical and critical ranges and, in one and two space dimensions, rapidly growing nonlinearities including double exponentials. a key ingredient in this analysis is a positive lower bound for the normalized solution at interior blow-up points. in fact, under weaker assumptions on the nonlinearity, we prove this bound in arbitrary space dimension without assuming radial symmetry.

title: ${\mathcal r}$-boundedness of riesz transforms and spectral multipliers of schrödinger operators
abstract: let $\ll = -δ+ v$ be a schrödinger operator with a non-negative potential. it is known that its associated riesz transform $\nabla \ll^{-\sfrac{1}{2}}$ is bounded on $l^p(\rr^d)$ for $p \in (1,2]$, with a bound independent of $v$. we prove more, namely that the set \[ \{ \nabla \ll^{-\sfrac{1}{2}},\ 0 \le v \in l^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\rr^d) \} \] is ${\mathcal r}$-bounded on $l^p(\rr^d)$ for $p \in (1,2]$. we also prove the ${\mathcal r}$-boundedness on $l^p(\rr^d)$, for $p \in (1,\infty)$, of the spectral multipliers \[ { m(\ll),\ 0 \le v \in l^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\rr^d) } \] for any $m:[0, \infty) \to \cc$ satisfying a hörmander type condition.   our approach is based on the analysis of schrödinger operators $-{\bf δ} + {\bf v}$ on vector-valued spaces $l^p(\rr^d,\ell^2)$. in particular, we prove heat kernel estimates, riesz transform bounds, and spectral multiplier results.

title: weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for riesz transforms of elliptic operators and magnetic schrödinger operators
abstract: let $m$ be a complete riemannian manifold and define a magnetic schrödinger operator $\ll = ({\bf d}+ ia)^*({\bf d}+ia) + v$ where $a$ is a real $1$-differential form in $l^2_{loc}$ and $v \in l^1_{loc}$ is a nonnegative electric potential.   we prove that the magnetic riesz transform $({\bf d} + ia) \ll^{-\einhalb}$ is of weak type $(1,1)$ with bound at most $2$. it extends to a bounded operator on $l^p$ for $p \in (1, 2]$ with norm bounded by a constant $c_p$ depending only on $p$. it is then independent of the dimension of the manifold and independent of $a$ and $v$. we also prove weak type $(1,1)$ bounds for symmetric elliptic operators subject to various boundary conditions on rough domains of $\rr^d$. the proofs are based on a new weak type $(1,1)$ criterion for operators.

title: global well-posedness of the energy-critical nonlinear schrödinger equation on the three-dimensional torus with additive lévy noise
abstract: this paper establishes global well-posedness for the defocusing energy-critical nonlinear schrödinger equation on the three-dimensional torus with a class of additive lévy noises. for arbitrary deterministic initial data in the energy space, we construct probabilistically strong solutions that are pathwise unique in the critical solution class. continuous dependence on initial data, convergence of finite-activity approximations, and a vanishing-noise limit hold on finite time intervals. when the effective noise is nonzero, quantitative bounds for mass exit times imply almost-sure unboundedness of the mass and exclude free scattering. the expected energy then admits a cubic lower bound in time. the analysis couples pathwise critical perturbation theory with energy estimates adapted to poisson compensation and stopping-time arguments based on the exact mass balance.

title: on blow-up for the supercritical defocusing nonlinear scalar wave equation
abstract: we study finite-time singularity formation for the scalar defocusing nonlinear wave equation $-\partial_t^2u+δu=u^p$. first, for fixed $d\geq4$ and odd $p\geq3$, we establish a conditional blow-up result under the assumption that a smooth self-similar imploding profile exists for the leading-order relativistic euler system, with associated normalized coefficients satisfying quantitative analytic radius conditions. second, we verify both the profile and the analytic radius conditions in dimensions four and five for all sufficiently large odd $p$. using finite speed of propagation, we obtain a dimension-independent threshold $p_0$ such that, for every $d\geq4$ and every odd $p\geq p_0$, finite-time blow-up occurs for some smooth, compactly supported, real-valued initial data. the proof combines a normalized formulation that separates the leading periodic oscillation from the unknown modulation, growth of the spatial analytic radius induced by an outgoing property, and frequency-dependent matrix multipliers that control the cumulative growth caused by the periodic linearized potential.

title: resolvent expansions at all spectral thresholds for three-dimensional discrete schrödinger operators
abstract: this paper studies resolvent expansions at all four spectral thresholds for the discrete schrödinger operator $h=-δ+v $ on $\z^3$, where $δ$ denotes the discrete laplacian on $\mathbb{z}^3$ and $v(n)$ is a real-valued decaying potential of $\mathbb{z}^3$. at the thresholds 0, 4, 8, and 12, we first give a complete classification of the threshold types and derive the corresponding resolvent expansions in weighted $\ell^2$-spaces, including the non-generic cases of resonances and eigenvalues.   as a result, we establish the jensen-kato type time-decay estimates of the evolution $e^{ith} p_{ac}(h)$ to discrete schrödinger equations with thresholds singularities on $\z^3$, with decay $o(t^{-3/2})$ when all thresholds are regular and $o(t^{-1/2})$ otherwise. these results provide a three-dimensional lattice analogue of the jensen--kato classical analysis at zero energy threshold on $\mathbb{r}^3$.

title: refined blow-up behavior for semilinear heat equations with arbitrarily fast growing nonlinearities
abstract: we study radially nonincreasing, positive blow-up solutions of a class of superlinear heat equations in the non-scale-invariant setting. this class contains nonlinearities with arbitrarily fast, super-exponential growth.   under suitable structural assumptions on the nonlinearity, we derive the sharp global blow-up profile in the original space-time variables.   more precisely, for positive nonlinearities $f$ satisfying $$   \lim_{x\to \infty}f'(x)g(x)= q\ge1\quad \quad   \hbox{ where }\quad\quad g(x)=\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{ ds}{f(s)}<\infty\quad\forall\ x>0, $$ and assuming either the time monotonicity $u_t\ge0$ holds or $q>\frac{p_s}{p_s-1}$, we have   $$   u(x,t)=(1+o(1))\,g^{-1}\bigg(t-t+\frac{|x|^2}{4q|\log |x|^2|}\bigg),   \quad \hbox{as $(x,t)\to (0,t)$.} $$ this estimate in particular provides the sharp final space profile and the corresponding refined space-time profile. moreover, our result recovers the universal structure of the global blow-up profile, given by the resolvent $g^{-1}$ of the associated ode evaluated at a time-space building block, which only depends on the limit $q$.

title: quantized slow blowup dynamics for the energy-critical schrödinger map flow
abstract: we study the cauchy problem for the energy-critical schrödinger map into the 2-sphere:   \[   \partial_{t}u = u\timesδu,   \quad (t,x)\in\mathbb{r}^{1+2},   \quad u(t,x)\in\mathbb{s}^2   \]   for equivariant initial data of homotopy degree $k=1$. given any integer $l\in\mathbb{n}_+$, we exhibit a set of initial data arbitrarily close to the ground state harmonic map in the energy norm such that the corresponding solution blows up in finite time with a quantized rate   \[   λ(t)\sim \frac{\left(t-t\right)^l}{\left|\log(t-t)\right|^{\frac{2l}{2l-1}}}   \quad\mbox{as}\ \ t\uparrow t.   \]   our proof is inspired by the techniques developed for the energy-critical harmonic map heat flow in a similar context by rapha{ë}l and schweyer~[anal. pde 7 (2014), 1713--1805]. however, its adaptation to a schrödinger-type equation requires the introduction of a new energy-virial-morawetz lyapunov functional tailored to quantized slow blowup dynamics.

title: transference principles for divergence sets of dispersive equations and their applications
abstract: in this article, we study the fractal refinement of the carleson's problem: (1) we introduce an equivalence relation on linear dispersive pdes on $\mathbb{r}^{n}$ based on the high-frequency oscillation of their fourier multipliers, proving that equations in the same class share the same hausdorff dimension of divergence sets. as applications, we estimate these dimensions for abstract dispersive families. consequently, we recover known $1$-dimensional results for linearized boussinesq and beam propagations, while establishing new results for both in higher dimensions and for klein-gordon propagations in all dimensions. (2) next, we study the effect of radial symmetry by obtaining dimension estimates for fractional schrödinger equations with concave phase and radial initial data. applying a transference principle, dimension estimates are extended to families of abstract dispersive equations. as special cases, we recover the known result for the beam propagation and also obtain new results for the linearized boussinesq and the klein-gordon propagations in the radial setting. (3) we study analogues of (2) for the $3$-dimensional real hyperbolic space by obtaining dimension estimates for a wide class of dispersive propagations: the schrödinger, fractional schrödinger (with convex and concave phases), beam, linearized boussinesq, wave and klein-gordon equations. this is the first result of its kind, outside the setting of flat euclidean geometry. our arguments are based on an inter-spatial transference principle of geometric-analytic flavour. in the process, we also obtain a quantitative result on the singular sets of sobolev functions, in the spirit of žubrinić, which may be of independent interest.

title: pauli-type coupling between spinors and curved spacetime
abstract: we investigate pauli-type interactions generated by minimal coupling of a specified covariantly regular representative of the dirac lagrangian. a derivative-quadratic term proportional to a length parameter $\ell$ is a total divergence in free flat spacetime and leaves the free dirac equation unchanged. after electromagnetic coupling, it is equivalent, up to a divergence, to a pauli operator with coefficient $-q\ell/6$. we explain how a specified comparison between measured and predicted anomalous magnetic moments constrains this coefficient, separating historical illustrative scales from a conditional statistical bound. in metric-compatible riemann--cartan spacetime, the same construction generates torsion-dependent derivative couplings and a spin-curvature coupling. in the torsion-free limit, the latter reduces to the scalar mass coefficient $m+\ell r/12$. on prescribed pure-axial and pure-vector torsion backgrounds, the characteristic form admits superluminal wavefronts relative to the spacetime metric in its nonzero-torsion lorentzian regime; sufficiently large spacelike effective torsion instead leads to degeneracy and an ultrahyperbolic characteristic form. for the observed cosmological constant and illustrative microscopic values of $\ell$, the vacuum mass correction is negligible. high-curvature applications and the characteristic structure of the full coupled theory require a specified gravitational action and further dynamical analysis.

title: a note on kinematic flow and differential equations for two-site one-loop graph in frw spacetime
abstract: in this work, we systematically study the differential systems governing loop-level wavefunction coefficients of conformally-coupled scalar field theory within a general power-law frw cosmology. by utilizing the twisted cohomology, hyperplane arrangements, and ibp techniques, we derive the canonical differential equations for two-site one-loop bubble and tadpole systems, revealing distinct structural differences. we present new insights into the one-loop tadpole system, uncovering that its integral family can include multiple parent functions due to distinct pairs of relative hyperplanes associated with each function, unlike the single parent function appearing in the one-loop bubble case. moreover, we demonstrate that the tadpole correlator selectively probes only a subset of the cohomology space, despite the hyperplane arrangement suggesting a higher-dimensional structure. another novel contribution of this work is the extension of kinematic flow framework to the loop-level scenarios for the first time. using a graphical approach based on family trees generated by marked tubing graphs, which encode singularity structures, we efficiently construct the differential equations and uncover the hierarchical relationships among the associated master integrals. additionally, we provide a preliminary discussion on generalization to two-site higher-loop configurations. we propose a general decomposition formula for the canonical form of a two-site diagram with arbitrary loops, breaking it into unshifted and shifted components associated with the fundamental tree-level and bubble-like structures, and establish a block-wise decomposition rule for the matrix $a$ in the corresponding differential system. these advancements provide a unified framework for two-site loop-level correlators and lay the groundwork for future study of more complex multi-site loop systems.

title: nonoscillatory gravitational quasinormal modes of reissner-nordström-de sitter spacetime
abstract: we revisit quasinormal modes of reissner-nordström-de sitter black holes, a classical and seemingly well-understood solution of einstein-maxwell theory with a positive cosmological constant. while previous studies have focused almost exclusively on the oscillatory photon-sphere branch, we show that two additional branches of nonoscillatory, purely imaginary modes - associated with the de sitter horizon and with the regime of near-extremal charge (zero-damped) - are essential for a complete description of the spectrum. these modes have so far remained largely unexplored for gravitational perturbations despite their relevance for late-time dynamics and stability. in particular, we derive accurate analytic expressions for the purely imaginary quasinormal frequencies in the slow-damping regime, providing a complete description of this sector of the spectrum.

title: probing scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves in the nhz band: nanograv and ska
abstract: scalar-induced gravitational waves (sigws) have recently attracted considerable interest, both as a possible explanation for the nanohertz signal reported by the pulsar timing array (pta) collaboration and for their connection with primordial black hole (pbh) physics. in addition to sigws, scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves (stgws) have emerged as a promising cosmological source of the stochastic gravitational wave background (sgwb). in this paper, we compute the stgws generated during a generic matter-dominated (md) era, as well as during an early matter-dominated (emd) epoch followed by a sudden transition to the standard radiation-dominated (rd) stage, working in the poisson gauge. we find that, in a purely md age, the corresponding energy density rapidly dilutes, whereas in the presence of an emd phase it remains non-vanishing due to the short duration of the emd period. we then investigate whether the stgw signal could provide a dominant contribution to the \texttt{nanograv 15-year} dataset and we forecast the prospects for its detection with future observations by the square kilometre array (ska). in particular, we consider stgws generated during both emd and rd eras, including their linear-order contributions. we further inject the scalar-induced contribution, both as an additional component and as the only signal, and compare the spectra against the same datasets. our results show that, although the sigws still appear to provide the dominant contribution and the posteriors are tightly constrained by the requirement of avoiding pbh overproduction, the gws induced by scalar-tensor mixing constitute a viable target for future, more sensitive nano-hz detectors of the sgwb.

title: impact of the einstein telescope's duty cycle on the estimation of binary black holes parameters
abstract: the geometry of the einstein telescope, the proposed next-generation european gravitational-wave observatory, is yet to be finalized. two competing designs are under consideration: a nested triangular configuration (et-δ) and two separated l-shaped detectors (et-2l). extensive prior comparisons of et designs established the scientific landscape using the fisher-information-matrix formalism and identified that duty-cycle-induced single-detector operation is precisely the regime where this approximation becomes less reliable, underscoring the need for a refined, principled treatment of the duty cycle. in this manuscript, we build on that foundation by revisiting the comparison with full bayesian parameter estimation of gravitational-wave signals from binary black-hole mergers, projected onto a simulated einstein telescope that incorporates a refined duty cycle modelled via continuous-time markov chains and testing different detector maintenance strategies. we find that the redundancy inherent in the et-δ design enables it to maintain at least two operational detectors for the majority of the observing time, whereas the et-2l configuration is often limited to a single detector. crucially, we show that, during partial network operation, et-δ often outperforms et-2l, and that the increased multi-detector uptime translates into tighter constraints on the luminosity distance and source-frame component masses. notably, this remains true even when gravitational-wave events have a lower signal-to-noise ratio in et-δ than in et-2l.

title: universal closed form for dynamical love numbers of black holes
abstract: black hole static love numbers vanish, but their dynamical counterparts do not. we present the entire scheme-independent dynamical response $\bar{f}_{\ell,s}$ of a schwarzschild black hole in closed form, to all orders in $g$, and for every spin $s$ and multipole $\ell$. the result is $\bar{f}_{\ell,s}/4πr_s^{2\ell+1}=φ_{\ell,s}(\bar{y})-\tfrac12η\,φ_{\ell,s}'(\bar{y})$ with $\bar{y}=-\tfrac12η^2τ$ and $η=iωr_s$. here $φ_{\ell,s}$ is simply the leading-log solution to the renormalization group equation, but lifting the running logarithm to $τ=\log(r_s/r)-2\sum_{k\ge2}ζ_k\,η^{k-1}$ resums it to all orders. this tower of riemann zeta values is the newtonian phase in disguise: it originates from the long-range $1/r$ potential in the far zone, and is universal across multipole and spin. our result exhibits a factorization pinned to three ingredients: the strength of horizon absorption, the running rate in the near zone, and the dressed logarithm in the far zone. using shell effective field theory, we independently verify our formula for scalar, electromagnetic, and gravitational perturbations, reaching $\mathcal o(g^{15})$.

title: separation of gravitational perturbations of singly spinning myers-perry black holes
abstract: gravitational perturbations of rotating black holes in higher dimensions generally obey coupled partial differential equations. we show that scalar gravitational perturbations invariant under rotations of the transverse sphere of a singly spinning myers-perry black hole separate, despite the obstruction to a decoupled teukolsky equation. two commuting, second-order angular operators organise the three gauge-invariant curvature components into joint eigenfunctions. the physical radial problem is a $2\times2$ first-order system, equivalent to a single second-order equation. this gives a separation of the sector containing both the bar-mode and axisymmetric ultraspinning instabilities. using only ordinary differential equations, we compute the bar-mode quasinormal spectrum in $d=5,6,7$ and find instability onsets at $a/r_+=0.90498$ and $0.83228$ in $d=6,7$. we also compute the growing axisymmetric modes and their onset rotations in $d=6,\ldots,9$. the construction shows how separability can survive the coupling between gravitational polarisations.

title: strong field gravitational lensing in full wave optics
abstract: compact binaries evolving in the vicinity of massive black holes may be commonplace in the universe, and their gravitational waves carry signatures of their environment. we study the strong lensing of these signals by the massive companion, a configuration that violates the standard assumptions of the lensing literature: geometric optics and thin lenses. using a perturbative framework, we compute the full wave optics amplification factors for face-on and edge-on binaries, including spinning lenses. in the edge-on configuration, peak amplification does not occur at perfect source--lens--observer alignment, even for a non-spinning lens. this is a consequence of the anisotropic, coherent quadrupolar emission of the stellar-mass binary breaking the axisymmetry of the system. restricting to the equatorial plane near the optical axis, we then find that the frequency dependence of the amplification factor is universal across every configuration studied, persisting deep into the wave optics regime. comparing against a strong-field ray tracing calculation, we find agreement at the $\sim10\%$ level for a face-on binary lensed by a schwarzschild black hole. in the less symmetric edge-on case only the angular peak shift and fringe spacing is reproduced to this accuracy. for a kerr lens, the face-on amplification factor is described by its schwarzschild counterpart to the same $\sim 10 \%$ accuracy once the effect of frame dragging is corrected for. a point mass lens, by contrast, fails to reproduce the features of the system, which may have strong implications for forecasts that adopt it for lensing by massive black holes in the strong field.

title: identity crisis: untangling mass-ordering artifacts from compact-object pairing in gravitational-wave populations
abstract: mass distributions of binary black hole mergers inferred from gravitational-wave observations offer clues to how binaries form. these distributions conventionally label the heavier component as the primary, with mass $m_1$, and the lighter as the secondary, with mass $m_2$, such that $m_1 \geq m_2$. this ordering folds the physically labeled mass distribution along the equal-mass line, potentially reshaping the underlying population structure. in this letter, we determine which population features can arise from mass ordering and which require genuine astrophysical structure. we show that ordering alone can produce (1) an $m_2$ distribution that declines more rapidly than the $m_1$ distribution, without intrinsic differences between the physically labeled components, and (2) an apparent concentration along equal masses, without correlations that preferentially pair black holes of equal mass. moreover, different physically labeled populations can produce the same ordered mass distribution. crucially, however, a preferred companion mass that remains constant as $m_1$ increases requires a characteristic mass scale already present in the physically labeled population. applied to binary black hole mergers in the fifth gravitational-wave transient catalog, our model recovers such a scale near $m_2 \simeq 50\,\mathrm{m}_\odot$. around this scale, the merger-rate density declines much more rapidly toward higher $m_2$ than toward lower $m_2$, ruling out an equal or weaker high-$m_2$ decline at 99.45% credibility. this structure therefore requires a characteristic mass scale in at least one physically labeled component, but masses alone cannot determine which component carries it. any formation model reproducing the observed high-mass binary black hole merger population must contain such a scale.

title: emris in kerr spacetime: the role of inclination diffusion
abstract: extreme mass ratio inspirals (emris) are expected to be a major source of gravitational waves (gws) for the future {\it laser interferometer space antenna} ({\it lisa}). an emri occurs when a compact object, driven by the emission of gravitational radiation, slowly inspirals into a massive black hole (mbh). the classical formation channel involves repeated two-body interactions within dense nuclear star clusters. however, both emri event rates and the expected distribution of their orbital parameters remain highly uncertain. a major source of this uncertainty is the poorly constrained ratio between gradually inspiraling emris and direct plunges, which do not produce detectable gws. while most studies of astrophysical emri production focus on the schwarzschild limit, previous work examining the kerr metric found that the spin of the central mbh can significantly affect the emri-to-plunge ratio. this enhancement depends sensitively on orbital inclination, yet earlier studies held inclination fixed. in this work, we develop the mathematical framework describing inclination evolution driven by two-body encounters evolving along kerr geodesics. by implementing 3d diffusion into monte carlo simulations, we show that initially prograde orbits may evolve into retrograde states, thereby converting potential emris into plunges or vice versa. we estimate the emri-to-plunge ratio and find that substantial mbh spin enhances the emri rate by a factor of $\sim 2.5$. additionally, even for a non-spinning mbh, modeling the orbits as relativistic geodesics rather than newtonian trajectories increases the number of emris by a similar factor of $\sim 2.5$. the distribution of kerr emri inclinations has a substantial prograde bias that may aid in identifying the subset of loss cone emris within large future emri samples.

title: strong-field gravitational-wave lensing from ray-traced arrival-time surfaces
abstract: the diffraction integral formalism has been greatly successful in describing gravitational wave lensing effects in scenarios where the wavelength of the signal is comparable to the characteristic length scale of the lens, known as the wave optics regime. however, the assumptions required to construct its integrand break down as the source approaches the strong gravity region of a black hole lens. in particular, we are interested in the lensed signal from a binary (the source) near a massive black hole (the lens). we present a new formalism for obtaining low frequency corrections to sources being lensed in the strong field regime of gravity by leveraging the fact that null geodesics obey the hamilton--jacobi equations. in doing so, we are able to construct a time delay surface without relying on the thin lens approximation, and solve the diffraction integral for the resulting surface directly. for a stationary source at $10m$, deep in the strong field regime, when comparing the results with a relativistic wave scattering model, we find $6.5\%$ and $0.3\%$ agreement in the peak amplification and first diffractive fringe, respectively. furthermore, we find a $< 1\%$ agreement with the amplitude of the point mass lens with a source at $10^4 m$ in the weak field, but noticeable dephasing between the peaks of the amplification function at higher frequencies. this work allows for clean interpolation between otherwise separate regimes, valid for sources from $\sim 6m \to \infty$. it provides a transparent, physically motivated framework for computing beyond-geometric optics lensing effects in the strong field regime.

title: scalar-assisted growth of supermassive black holes: boson-mass windows and observational constraints
abstract: we study a phenomenological cosmological model of black-hole growth in which a finite baryonic reservoir and a bosonic scalar cloud feed the black hole simultaneously. the baryonic component accretes through an eddington-like channel, while the scalar cloud transfers mass through an effective quasibound-state decay rate. evolving the system directly in redshift within a flat $λ$cdm background, we scan over $μ$, $m_0$, $m_{c,0}$, and $m_{b,0}$ to assess whether scalar-assisted accretion can accelerate the formation of $10^9m_\odot$ supermassive black holes. we find that the scalar contribution is highly selective in parameter space. for the mass scales explored here, scalar transfer is most efficient for $μ\sim10^{-19}-10^{-16} \mathrm{ev}$, producing rapid cloud depletion and significantly earlier black-hole growth, while outside this interval the evolution remains mainly baryonic. more generally, this efficient window reflects a preferred range of the dimensionless coupling $α=μm_{\rm bh}$ and therefore shifts approximately as $μ\propto m_{\rm bh}^{-1}$. comparison with observed quasar masses and luminosities instead favors lower boson masses, broadly around $μ\sim10^{-21}-10^{-20}\mathrm{ev}$. these results are not necessarily in tension, since the boson mass that maximizes early growth depends on the characteristic black-hole mass and evolutionary stage. this separation between dynamical efficiency and observational compatibility leaves open complementary roles for different bosonic mass scales in supermassive black hole growth and dark-matter phenomenology.

title: black hole fine structure
abstract: in general relativity, axial and polar black-hole perturbations share identical quasinormal-mode spectra, a property known as isospectrality. new physics can break this degeneracy, producing a spectral splitting analogous to atomic fine structure. we perform a theory-agnostic search for such splitting in gravitational-wave observations. we find no evidence for isospectrality breaking and place a combined $90\%$ upper limit of $<28.5\%$ on the relative frequency splitting. we map these constraints onto several modified-gravity theories, constraining the coupling-lengths to be $\lesssim 28\,\mathrm{km}$.

title: linear stability matrix and lyapunov exponents for stationary spacetime
abstract: lyapunov exponents characterize the average rate at which nearby trajectories in phase space converge or diverge and therefore provide a useful criterion for dynamical stability. in this work, we develop a general framework for analyzing lyapunov exponents in stationary spacetimes and extend previous studies beyond circular orbits. for a generic stationary spacetime described by $g_{μν}(r,θ)$, we show that the phase space relevant to linear perturbations is spanned by $(r,p_r,θ,p_θ)$ and the corresponding linear stability matrix has rank four. when the spacetime admits a rank-2 killing tensor, the linear stability matrix can be reduced to a block-diagonal form, allowing the lyapunov exponents to be obtained analytically. by imposing the appropriate constraint conditions, the formalism further yields the linear stability matrices and lyapunov exponents for circular and spherical orbits. the validity of the method is illustrated by several representative examples, including the (inverted) harmonic oscillator, planar kepler motion, and particle motion in schwarzschild and kerr spacetimes. these results provide a unified framework for investigating the stability properties of particle orbits in both classical and relativistic dynamical systems.

title: detectability of gravitational waves from extreme-mass-ratio inspirals on periodic orbits around bardeen black holes
abstract: we investigate gravitational wave (gw) signatures from extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (emris) around a bardeen black hole, modeling the small object as a test particle, and provide a framework for probing strong-field spacetime geometry. we first present the equations of motion for test particles around a bardeen black hole and characterize circular orbits in the parameter space of energy and angular momentum. using levin's classification, we adopt the extended classification scheme to classify periodic orbits around a bardeen black hole. we then compute gw waveforms in both the time and frequency domains, as well as the corresponding characteristic strains, for these periodic orbits and compare them with the sensitivity curves of the laser interferometer space antenna (lisa), the evolved laser interferometer space antenna (elisa), the tianqin mission, the big bang observer (bbo), and the decihertz interferometer gravitational wave observatory (decigo). we find that detectability is controlled primarily by the luminosity distance. at a luminosity distance of 200 mpc, the signals can exceed the sensitivity curves of bbo and decigo and are comparable to the lisa sensitivity curve, whereas at 2 gpc, they remain below the sensitivity curves of all detectors considered. these results suggest that emris on periodic orbits around bardeen black holes offer a promising avenue to probe strong-field gravity and the properties of bardeen black holes.

title: hierarchical parameter estimation for intrinsic parameters of extreme-mass-ratio inspirals using deep learning
abstract: extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (emris) stand as prime targets for future space-borne gravitational wave (gw) detectors, yet their precise parameter estimation is severely hindered by waveform complexity and high-dimensional parameter spaces. in this work, we propose a deep learning framework capable of recovering the seven intrinsic emri parameters without relying on detailed priors for extrinsic parameters. our approach first employs a u-net to extract robust signal features from noisy time-frequency data. these features are then fed into a multi-channel convolutional neural network (cnn) equipped with a dual attention mechanism, which decouples the time and frequency dimensions to jointly model long-range temporal evolution and persistent spectral structures, thereby enhancing sensitivity to emri time-frequency ridges in noisy data. remarkably, this method reduces the search ranges for the parameters $\{\log m, a, μ, e_0, p_0 \}$ and $\{t_p, {x_i}_0 \}$ by factors of $\sim 10^{2}$ and $\sim 10^{1}$, respectively, effectively shrinking the total volume of the seven-dimensional parameter space by $\sim 10^{8}$. such a dramatic reduction enables a rapid pre-screening of the intrinsic parameter space, substantially saving computational cost for subsequent full parameter estimation. although our framework is developed with taiji mission specifications in mind, the methodology is applicable to data from other space-borne gw detectors.

title: a catalog of long, eccentric and precessing binary black hole simulations from icts-tifr
abstract: we present a catalogue of 31 binary black hole simulations performed with the spectral einstein code (spec) on the sonic cluster at icts-tifr, bengaluru between august 2023 and december 2024, targeting the sparsely covered corner of parameter space in which orbital eccentricity and spin-orbit precession are present simultaneously: 17 configurations are both eccentric and precessing, spanning mass ratios $1 \le q \le 11$ and initial eccentricities up to $\hat{e}_0 = 0.40$. the longest, eccprecdiff002, inspirals for 80 orbits (159 gravitational-wave cycles), to our knowledge the longest simultaneously eccentric and precessing binary black hole evolution to date.   compile-time optimisation of spec and its third-party library stack for the amd zen-2 architecture delivered a 90% speedup of the initial-data solver and a 40% speedup of the evolution, roughly half of the latter traceable to a single defect in how pre-2.34 glibc reported cache topology on amd processors. the campaign consumed $1.18 \times 10^{6}$ cpu-hours.   we document the post-processing pipeline and validate the frame transformation and waveforms. eccentricity is measured from the waveforms and compared against the initial data. the first law of binary black hole mechanics, a test of approximate helical symmetry, is satisfied to better than 0.54% for every configuration with $e_ω < 0.2$, and we show that even precessing systems can be regarded as possessing approximate helical symmetry in the co-precessing frame. using the aligned-spin simulations to calibrate the numerical floor, the co-precessing approximation's mirror-symmetry violation lies three to four ordersof magnitude above it, growing from 0.7% to 5.3%with opening angle. eccprecdiff002 spans the band above 5 hz without hybridisationfor $m \le 62\,m_\odot$, giving a single-interferometer signal-to-noise ratio of 961 in cosmic explorer at 1 gpc.

title: testing charged black holes embedded in anisotropic matter and surrounded by plasma through gravitational lensing: bounds from the sloan lens acs survey
abstract: we investigate weak gravitational lensing by a charged black hole surrounded by anisotropic matter, described by the two-component kiselev metric, and immersed in a homogeneous plasma. we first examine the black hole geometry and horizon structure and then derive the weak-deflection angle from the hamiltonian description of light propagation in plasma, using an expansion with a fixed turning point that we verify against direct numerical integration. using the gravitational lens equation, we obtain the einstein-ring angle, the image positions, the total magnification and the fractional magnifications of the primary and secondary images. we then confront the model with the einstein radii of two galaxy-scale lenses of the sloan lens acs survey, j0008$-$0004 and j0029$-$0055. because the einstein angle cannot be smaller than the reduced deficit deflection, the observed radii give the mass-independent bounds $k<6.5\times10^{-6}$ and $k<4.2\times10^{-6}$, respectively. the charge correction to the einstein radius is suppressed by $r_s/r_e\approx 5\times10^{-6}$ and is unobservable, while the plasma parameter at the optical wavelengths of the slacs imaging is of order $10^{-22}$ and cannot be constrained. our results show that galaxy-scale strong lensing data place stringent limits on anisotropic matter surrounding the lens, whereas plasma effects can be probed only at low radio frequencies.

title: all quiet on the vector front: scalar growth and perturbative control in horndeski--weyl-squared gravity
abstract: higher-order curvature corrections to general relativity arise naturally in many fundamental theories and provide phenomenologically interesting low-energy effective field theories. however, higher-derivative terms can introduce ghost modes, which call the validity of such models into question. here, we thoroughly investigate the classical linear stability of the most general second-order scalar-tensor theory, namely the horndeski theory of gravity, augmented by a weyl-squared term in the action. we consider shift-symmetric de sitter and power-law flrw backgrounds and study the evolution of linear perturbations. vector perturbations are free of gradient and tachyonic instabilities for a positive weyl-induced mass squared. tensor perturbations necessarily contain a ghost; their superhorizon branches are bounded, while a frozen-background calculation identifies a separate finite-momentum stability condition. the scalar sector instead contains a growing long-wavelength branch for all expanding backgrounds we consider, which is inherited by at least one of the gauge-invariant bardeen potentials. we show that this growth enters the bardeen potentials through an inverse-gradient factor $a^2/k^2$: the dynamical scalar fields remain bounded on the inflationary backgrounds, the direct contribution of the growing shear to the clock-matched tidal field cancels, and the electric part of the weyl tensor decays. we discuss the implications of our results for perturbative control and for the phenomenological viability of theories including quadratic curvature corrections.

title: correlation between gravitational wave frequencies as a signature of new black hole physics
abstract: we point out that for black holes (bh) of the same mass, despite of arising from two entirely different physical arguments, the peak frequency of the coarse-grained gravitational wave (gw) spectrum of gravitons $f_\text{peak}^\text{graviton}$ is very close to the peak frequency of the gw spectrum produced from binary bh mergers $f_\text{peak}^\text{merger}$. in particular, we find that $f_\text{peak}^\text{graviton}/f_\text{peak}^\text{merger}\approx 2.3$ independent from bh mass or population. if bhs are still evaporating, the peak frequencies scale as $\propto m_i^{-1}$ with $m_i$ is the initial bh mass. if bhs evaporated in the radiation (matter) dominated era, the peak frequencies scale as $\propto m_i^{1/2}$ ($\propto m_i$) respectively after taking into account redshift effect. any deviation from the aforementioned magical ratio would indicate new bh physics. the sweetest frequency ballpark to look for this correlation is around $10^{14}\ \rm hz-10^{20}\ \rm hz$ where both gw spectra are allowed to have maximum amplitude. as a demonstration of what the new physics could be, we consider a phenomenological self-similar regular bh model of hayward featuring a single hair parameter. the observed ratio of peak frequencies can be used to directly infer the hair parameter, along with crucial properties of the novel bh solution such as hawking temperature, horizon size, and innermost stable circular orbit. we also comment on the pros and cons of correlating frequencies among other gw sources such as formation, population fluctuation, and sudden transition of adiabatic perturbation.

title: biases in ringdown tests of general relativity from gravitational-wave microlensing
abstract: gravitational-wave (gw) ringdown signals provide a powerful probe of the strong-field regime of general relativity (gr) through black hole spectroscopy and tests of the kerr hypothesis. however, unmodeled propagation effects can bias the inference of remnant properties and the interpretation of ringdown features. we investigate the impact of gravitational lensing on ringdown inference and tests of gr using gw150914-like simulated signals spanning the long-wavelength, wave-optics, and geometric-optics regimes. we perform complementary time-domain post-merger and frequency-domain full inspiral--merger--ringdown analyses using unlensed waveform models. we find that lensing in the wave-optics regime can produce substantial biases in the inferred remnant mass and spin and can strongly affect the inferred modal content of the ringdown. in particular, it can spuriously favor the presence of the first overtone, with $\log_{10}\mathcal{b}^{221}_{220}\sim40$, even though the injected signal has no support for it. parameterized ringdown tests can likewise yield strong apparent support for deviations from the kerr quasinormal mode (qnm) spectrum, with $\log_{10}\mathcal{b}^{\rm modgr}_{\rm gr}\sim8$. in contrast, the evidence for higher-order modes remains largely unchanged for the simulated signals considered here. the parameterized analysis using the entire signal further shows that microlensing can bias the inferred frequency of the dominant $(2,2,0)$ qnm. these results demonstrate that unmodeled microlensing can produce systematic biases and spurious signatures in ringdown analyses, potentially affecting precision tests of the kerr hypothesis.

title: search for compact binary coalescences with sub-solar mass components in data from the second part of ligo-virgo-kagra's fourth observing run
authors: j. f. j. van den brand
abstract: we report on a gravitational wave search for compact binary coalescences with secondary mass between 0.2 m and 1 m and primary mass between 0.2 m and 10 m, restricting the component mass ratio to lie between 0.1 and 1. the analysis uses data collected by the ligo and virgo detectors between 2024 april 10 15:00:00 and 2025 january 28 17:00:00, the second part of the fourth observing run of the ligo-virgo-kagra collaboration. results from two out of three search pipelines show outlier candidates, but not at a sufficient level of significance to provide evidence for detection. we report the combined sensitivity of the current searches over the first and second parts of the observing run to the target sub-solar mass (ssm) black hole (bh) population, as well as to neutron star (ns) binaries with one or more sub-solar component. we place upper limits on the merger rate of ssm bhs, ranging from $50 {\rm gpc}^{-3} {\rm yr}^{-1}$ to~$5000 {\rm gpc}^{-3} {\rm yr}^{-1}$ (90% confidence) for different component mass combinations. we use the merger rate limits to constrain two illustrative dark matter (dm) scenarios that can form ssm compact objects: primordial bhs, and dark bhs forming in a dissipative dm model. our search limits the fraction of dm in primordial bhs, assuming a monochromatic mass distribution, to be $\leq$ (0.018-0.032) at 1 m, and $\leq$ (0.10-0.18) at 0.35 m for early-forming binaries; or to be less than 1 at masses above (0.62-0.74) m for late-forming binaries. for the dissipative model, we constrain the fraction of dm for a range of minimum dark black hole masses below $1\,m$ to be as low as (1.0-1.1) x $10^{-5}$; we also exclude minimum masses above (0.62-0.74) m, if dark bhs constitute all of the dm. for binary nss that include sub-solar mass components, assuming a simple, fixed population model we find a merger rate upper limit of $249 {\rm gpc}^{-3} {\rm yr}^{-1}$.

title: analytical time-domain waveforms for black-hole scattering in the self-force expansion
abstract: we obtain a systematic understanding of the time-domain gravitational waveform of hyperbolic black-hole scattering at first order in the self-force expansion and all orders in the post-newtonian/post-minkowskian (pn/pm) expansion. the continuous frequency spectrum of unbound orbits makes the inverse fourier transform to the time domain diverge order by order; we introduce a dimensional-regularization-inspired prescription that cures this uniformly. we show that the full waveform then follows, at any pm and pn order, from a single family of integrals, generated by the lauricella function $f_d^{(3)}$, which we calculate using strategies familiar from the study of feynman integrals. as a proof of principle, we use this understanding to compute the quadrupolar 1sf waveform through relative 10pm-20pn, that is to order ${\cal o}(g^{10} v^{42})$, the full 1sf waveform to 10pm-10pn, as well as the asymptotic fluxes and the dissipative scattering angle at the corresponding accuracy.

title: analytical time-domain waveforms for black-hole scattering in the post-minkowskian expansion
abstract: we present the first analytic computation of the time-domain multipoles of the gravitational waveform from hyperbolic black-hole scattering at leading order in the post-minkowskian expansion, to all orders in velocity. we perform the partial-wave projection as a cut loop integral, which enables the use of dimensional regularization and associated integration techniques. as opposed to the frequency domain, the time-domain multipoles are logarithmic and do not contain bessel-like functions. our results pave the way for the incorporation of post-minkowskian fluxes in waveform models for binary mergers.

title: cubic quasinormal modes in the black-hole ringdown
abstract: we formulate and numerically solve the nonlinear teukolsky equations through third order, obtaining a first-principles calculation of cubic quasinormal-mode amplitudes for kerr black holes. our approach combines lower-order metric reconstruction in split light-cone gauges with a hyperboloidal, compactified formulation solved on complex radial contours. spin-dependent complex coupling coefficients fix the cubic amplitudes from products of their linear parent amplitudes. we apply these predictions to a nonprecessing numerical-relativity waveform, including cubic products of the $(2,2)$ fundamental mode, its first overtone, and their conjugates. the predicted cubic terms improve agreement over selected early-ringdown fitting windows and shift inferred linear-overtone amplitudes without adding fitting parameters. $3m$ after the peak of $|h_{22}|$, the summed cubic contribution reaches approximately $38\%$ of the total $h_{22}$ signal; $m$ is the initial total mass. these results identify an appreciable cubic response in early ringdown.

title: binary-lens amplification of starlight: from magnification flares to quasi-periodic tracking of orbital evolution
abstract: supermassive black hole binaries (smbhb) are expected at the center of galaxies as a result of galaxy mergers. the dynamics and evolution of smbhbs shed light on the evolution and formation of galaxies, the gravitational wave background and the nature of gravity. many methods have been proposed to identify sub-parsec smbhbs via the detection of gravitational waves or the modulation of the emission from the surrounding gaseous environment. in a previous study, we proposed a new method of identifying smbhbs in non-active galactic nuclei via gravitational lensing. the caustics, i.e. the source positions with a divergent magnification, exhibit a complex extended geometry which rotates with the binary period. each caustic-crossing produces an extreme magnification by up to a factor of $10^{6}$. in this work, we generalize the previous study and describe the rich phenomenology of binary-lens amplification of starlight (blast). we explore the electromagnetic transients produced when accounting for the relative proper motion of the source, either a single or a binary star, the eccentricity and precession of the smbhb, and the relative inclination. systems where a star rapidly drifts across the caustic produce a single- or double-peaked flare. in the opposite limit, a star with no relative proper motion produces quasi-periodic lensed starlight (qpls), i.e., repeated peaks that track the system's orbital evolution. we determine the expected magnification and peak duration in different circumstances, and calculate the magnification curves and their fourier transforms. this study may help construct search pipelines to identify smbhbs in electromagnetic time-domain surveys.

title: constraining the progenitor orbits of sequential black-hole mergers in hierarchical triples: peters-based estimates
abstract: two black-hole merger events may originate from sequential mergers in a pre-existing hierarchical black-hole triple if their spatial localizations overlap and the remnant mass of the first merger is compatible with a component mass of the second. in this scenario, the inner binary merges first, leaving a remnant that remains bound to the tertiary and subsequently undergoes a second merger. we present a method to constrain the progenitor triple's outer orbit by modeling the gravitational-wave-driven evolution of the remnant-tertiary binary using peters' equations. given an assumed upper bound on the recoil velocity of the first merger, the method requires only the black-hole masses, the time delay between the mergers, and the eccentricity at a reference frequency - quantities that can be inferred from the merger events themselves. we investigate the potential constraining power by constructing a constraint atlas spanning a range of system properties and identify the conditions under which the method places tight and reliable bounds on the progenitor triple's outer orbital parameters. by imposing an upper bound on the detector-band eccentricity, we also obtain meaningful constraints for candidate hierarchical mergers proposed in the literature, including gw190514-gw190521. we provide numerical tools for applying the method to user-specified systems and evaluating the reliability of the resulting peters-based constraints. this framework offers a computationally inexpensive first step toward reconstructing hierarchical-merger progenitors and provides a foundation for extensions incorporating more sophisticated relativistic treatments.
